Title: Building a great nation starts with happy families - PM
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: National development should not be measured solely by the grandeur of skyscrapers, technological advancements or an influx of investments, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said it must be anchored in the development of individuals who are civilised, possess good character and hold noble human values.
Anwar said efforts to build a great nation must begin with the establishment of happy family institutions.
"Families are the foundation of society and pillar of national strength, and as such, the concept of 'Menggapai di Langit, Mengakar di Bumi' (Reaching for the sky, Rooted in Ground) should serve as a guiding principle in educating the younger generation to master technology and new knowledge without neglecting values, manners, compassion and noble character.
"I am confident that efforts to build a great nation must begin with building happy families, because it is from the family institution that generations who will determine the face and future of the nation emerge," he said in a Facebook post.
The prime minister said the Madani Government would continue to strengthen policies and initiatives prioritising family well-being, including the welfare of mothers and children, childcare facilities, support for persons with disabilities (PwDs) and recognition of the role of caregivers.
Earlier, Anwar officiated the National Family Month 2026 celebration in Shah Alam, Selangor, today, which was also attended by his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, and Minister of Women, Family and Community Development Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri.
At the same time, the prime minister also commended Nancy and her ministry for successfully organising the celebration and their steadfast commitment to championing women's well-being and strengthening the family institution as a cornerstone of societal and national development.

Title: Myanmar plans April by-election, including in conflict areas
Article:
Myanmar's military-appointed election commission has scheduled by-elections for April next year to fill dozens of parliamentary seats, state media said on Friday, including in areas impacted by a protracted civil war.
The contest for vacant seats in 55 constituencies will be held on April 4, the Global New Light of Myanmar reported.
The vote follows a general election held in December and January that was won overwhelmingly by the military-backed Union Solidarity and Development Party in the absence of any viable opposition.
The election was criticised as a sham by the United Nations and many Western countries and led to junta chief Min Aung Hlaing becoming president.
The USDP currently controls 84% of the bicameral parliament.
Myanmar has been in turmoil since a 2021 coup triggered a civil war that has killed an estimated 100,000 people and displaced more than 3.5 million.
Several seats in the by-election will encompass townships in the Sagaing Region plus Chin and Shan states, where anti-military resistance forces have a strong presence.
Not included is restive Rakhine state, bordering Bangladesh, where the military is locked in fierce fighting with the rebel Arakan Army.
Voting in the general election was held in 692 constituencies, with 121 excluded as they were out of the military's control.
—REUTERS

Title: Nine detained over teen's fatal stabbing in Sibu
Article:
SIBU: Police have detained nine people, aged between 16 and 42, to assist a probe into the murder of a 19-year-old who is believed to have been stabbed during a fight at a public park in Jalan Gambir here early today.
Sibu district police chief ACP Abang Zainal Abidin Abang Ahmad said all suspects were rounded up at several locations around Sibu between 10am and 4pm today following intelligence gathering and investigations by the Sibu police headquarters' Criminal Investigation Department (CID).
He said police received a report at about 2am regarding a brawl where the complainant was assaulted by a group of people.
"During the incident, a young man was believed to have been stabbed with a sharp weapon and was confirmed dead by a medical team from Sibu Hospital," he said in a statement.
Abang Zainal Abidin said the incident had also gone viral on social media.
He said the case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder, which provides for the death penalty or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years, and not less than 12 strokes of the cane, upon conviction.
Police have also urged members of the public with information on the incident to come forward to assist in the investigation.

Title: Indonesian workers rally for Prabowo as women march against president
Article:
JAKARTA: Hundreds of workers rallied in support of Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto on Saturday amid allegations that police illegally wiretapped him, while hundreds of women marched against the president's policies.
The pro-Prabowo demonstration marked a contrast to recent protests against his administration, part of growing public discontent over his costly populist policies, handling of raging wildfires and weakening investor confidence in Southeast Asia's biggest economy.
Labour Party Chairperson Said Iqbal, leading the workers' rally, called for unity to support Prabowo and said he would mobilise union members against those who threaten the former general's presidency.
"We can mobilise members of our organisation across every town, every factory," Said, a special adviser to the president, was quoted as saying by Detik News. "We are prepared to respond at any moment to maintain order should any unrest arise, whether instigated by foreign interests or by individuals seeking to cause trouble."
Indonesian police have named four senior police officials as suspects accused of attempting to intercept Prabowo's communications, including a former police chief who is known as a loyalist of former president Joko Widodo.
The scandal has exposed deepening cracks between Prabowo and his predecessor and former backer, known as Jokowi.
Jokowi has said he respected the legal process. The lawyer for one of the four suspects said his client would cooperate with the investigation.
Also on Saturday, civil society groups held the women's march in Jakarta to demand more women's rights and protest against Prabowo's handling of the forest fires that have been raging for months, his costly free-meal programme and a tax on women's sanitary products.
There have been several protests launched against Prabowo in recent months, including student rallies last week in the capital and other cities. — REUTERS

Title: Melaka polls: MIC's sole candidate sacrifices family time to campaign for Gadek's future
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: For Barisan Nasional candidate for Gadek S. Nadarajah, this Deepavali will be unlike previous celebrations as his campaign commitments leave little time for family gatherings.
With the Melaka election campaign taking priority, even a planned lunch with his family remains uncertain as he continues making his rounds to meet voters.
As MIC's sole candidate in the election, Nadarajah said his focus was on engaging with voters, listening to their concerns and understanding issues affecting their daily lives.
He said he had only managed to call his father this morning to check on the family's Deepavali preparations.
"My focus is entirely on campaigning. I only managed to call my father this morning to ask about the family's Deepavali preparations.
"He told me everything was in order and that I should not worry about things at home.
"I told them perhaps they could come and meet me for lunch tomorrow, but even that has not been confirmed because I do not know where I will be at that time," he said when met while campaigning here.
Instead of spending time with his family, Nadarajah plans to visit temples and the homes of Indian voters in Gadek.
"Tomorrow, I will visit several temples in Gadek where the Hindu community will be celebrating Deepavali.
"I have also received invitations from several families in the constituency to visit their homes.
"That is how I will be spending my Deepavali. We will continue campaigning, but tomorrow's activities will be dedicated to the Indian community celebrating the festival," he said.
Reflecting on his first week on the campaign trail, Nadarajah described the response from voters as encouraging, although some had openly voiced their frustrations over unresolved local issues.
He said he welcomed the feedback, viewing it as an opportunity to better understand the problems facing the people.
"The campaign has been very good and satisfying so far. Wherever I go, people have welcomed me warmly.
"Of course, there are also those who express their frustrations, sometimes in a slightly raised voice.
"That is normal. When people face difficulties, they need an opportunity to express what is troubling them," he said.

Title: High-tide phenomenon may hit low-lying, coastal areas in Selangor tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Residents in low-lying and coastal areas of Selangor have been urged to remain vigilant following the forecast of a high tide phenomenon, with water levels expected to reach up to 5.2 metres (m) tomorrow.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director, Ashrul Riezal Asbar, said the forecast was based on projections by the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID), with water levels in Klang recorded at 5.1 metres today.
He said the situation could lead to water flows from the Sungai Buloh and Ijok areas to converge with the high tide, thereby increasing the risk of flooding in low-lying areas.
"As such, we urge residents in coastal and low-lying areas, such as around Kuala Selangor, to remain vigilant and make early preparations," he said.
Regarding the flooding in Kampung Melayu Subang today, Ashrul Riezal said the rising water levels in the area were believed to have been caused by overflow from the local drainage system, rather than the high tide phenomenon.
He said the Selangor Fire and Rescue Department had not received any further reports on the incident, but monitoring efforts were ongoing to ensure that any assistance required could be provided promptly.
Meanwhile, social media posts shared by users showed Kampung Melayu Subang being hit by flash floods again following heavy rain this afternoon, with water inundating residential areas and submerging parts of residents' yards and access roads.
A Threads user, Nurul Azuwana, claimed that water levels rose after only about 20 minutes of rain, while another use, hyenarawr1, claimed that it was the third flash flood to hit the area this week.
On Monday (Nov 2), about 92 houses in four areas in Kampung Melayu Subang, namely Lorong Merbau, Jalan Cengal, Jalan Resak and Jalan Jati, were reported to have been after by flooding.

Title: Fallen trees crush cars, damage shop in Kubang Semang and Prai
Article:
SEBERANG PRAI: Two separate fallen tree incidents damaged two vehicles, a house and a shop in Kubang Semang and Prai today.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department operations division assistant director John Sagun Francis said they were alerted to the incident in Prai at 6.01pm today.
A team from the Prai fire station, supported by personnel from the Bandar Perda fire station, was dispatched to the scene at Desa Sutera Square along Jalan Sutera 3.
"Firefighters found a fallen tree had crushed a Proton Saga taxi and damaged a small section of a nearby shop roof. The taxi driver, in his 50s, escaped unhurt.
"Firefighters, together with workers from the Seberang Prai City Council (MBSP), carried out cutting and clearing operations to remove the fallen trunk and branches," he said.
The operation ended at 7.57pm after the area was deemed safe and handed over to the local council for further action.
Francis said that in an earlier incident, firemen from the Penanti fire station were deployed to Mengkuang Titi in Kubang Semang after a tree fell and hit a Perodua Bezza and a portion of a house.
"The 24-year-old car owner was unhurt.
"Personnel cleared the tree before handing the site back to the homeowner," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Flash floods hit Seberang Prai Tengah after torrential downpour
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM: Several residential areas in Seberang Prai Tengah were inundated following a continuous downpour that lashed the district late this afternoon.
The affected areas include Seberang Jaya, Permatang Rawa, Tanah Liat, Mengkuang Titi and Jalan Baharu.
The Civil Defence Force (APM), which serves as the District Disaster Management Committee (JPBD) Secretariat, said response teams were deployed shortly after heavy rain began around 4.30pm.
"Community agents were activated to monitor the ground, and by 6.15pm, we received reports of drainage overflow and fallen trees in Seberang Jaya, with water entering several homes.
"However, the situation remains under control," it said.
At 7.30pm, authorities detected rising water levels in Mengkuang Titi.
"The Social Welfare Department is on standby should any evacuation become necessary, but as of 8pm, no temporary relief centres have been opened," it said.
Agencies involved in ongoing monitoring operations include the district office, police, Fire and Rescue Department, Drainage and Irrigation Department, and local community leaders.

Title: Pressure on Israel must go beyond proposed resolutions, says Zahid
Article:
ISTANBUL: The international community must take legal action against Israel to stop its military operations in Gaza, southern Lebanon and Syria.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said pressure on Israel must go beyond proposed resolutions and translate into concrete action to ensure it respects and complies with previously agreed ceasefires.
"Despite the change of leadership in Israel after the recent election, we find that, in terms of policy (on the ceasefire), it may not change.
"The involvement of the international community is needed to increase pressure on Israel, including through legal action and other measures, particularly among countries neighbouring it," he said in a press conference after a roundtable discussion with the Foundation for Political, Economic and Social Research (Seta) here.
The 11-member Seta delegation was led by its coordinator, Prof Nebi Mis, and included its foreign policy studies director, Prof Murat Yesiltas, and publications director Ebrar Uzumcu.
Zahid, who is also Umno president, said the party plans to collaborate with Seta on research through the Abdullah Badawi Research Institute to strengthen knowledge-sharing between Malaysia and Türkiye.
He said the cooperation could include the exchange of research materials produced by both institutions, while Seta also has ties with the Institute of Strategic and International Studies (ISIS) Malaysia.
Zahid said the sharing of expertise and research findings is expected to benefit both countries, particularly in understanding regional and global geopolitical and socioeconomic developments.
Seta is an independent, non-profit think tank that conducts research on political, economic and social issues in Türkiye and globally, covering foreign policy, security, economics, society, energy and technology.
The discussion was part of Zahid's four-day visit to Türkiye from Nov 5 to 8 for the two-day TRT World Forum 2026 at the Istanbul Congress Centre, which began yesterday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Four injured in Seberang Jaya multi-vehicle pile-up
Article:
SEBERANG JAYA: Four people were injured in a four-vehicle collision along Km134.8 of the North-South Expressway near Seberang Jaya this afternoon.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department operations division assistant director John Sagun Francis said they were alerted to the incident at 4.35pm.
A team of eight firefighters and a fire engine from the Prai station were dispatched to the scene.
"The accident involved four vehicles — two Perodua Myvi, a Toyota Alphard and a Honda Accord — with seven people involved in total," he said.
Francis said that of the seven people, four sustained light injuries.
"Two of the injured victims were travelling in the first Myvi, one in the second Myvi and one in the Honda Accord.
"The occupants of the Toyota Alphard escaped unhurt."
Operations personnel administered preliminary medical treatment to the victims at the scene before they were transported to Seberang Jaya Hospital via ambulances.
Firefighters also conducted site clean-up operations to clear accident debris from the expressway lanes.
Francis said the operation concluded at 5.37pm after ensuring the area was completely safe.
Police personnel were also present to assist with traffic management.

Title: Delhi world's most polluted major city on eve of Diwali, Swiss group says
Article:
BENGALURU: Delhi was the world's most polluted major city on Saturday morning, according to Swiss group IQAir's live ranking, as the Indian capital faced severe pollution forecasts a day before Diwali, the Hindu festival of lights.
* India has ordered schools in and around Delhi to offer online classes, and encouraged people to work from home ahead of Diwali on Sunday, which is usually marked by the widespread use of firecrackers that further worsen the air quality.
* IQAir ranked Delhi first among the world's major cities at 10:35am (0505 GMT), with a US air quality index reading of 581, double that of Lahore in neighbouring Pakistan, at 285.
* IQAir's reading, based on concentrations of air pollutants, is not directly comparable to India's official index, which uses a different scale and methodology.
* India's Central Pollution Control Board put Delhi's air quality index at 363 at 10 am, in the "very poor" category.
* Friday's air quality in Delhi was the worst pre-Diwali air in eight years, local media said, citing official data.
* Pollution ​is an annual problem in many parts of northern India from the onset of winter as ⁠cold, heavy air traps vehicle emissions, construction dust and smoke from crop-waste burning.
— REUTERS

Title: Mara signs two LoCs with Turkish universities
Article:
ISTANBUL: Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) has strengthened Malaysia–Turkiye academic ties through collaborations with two Turkish universities, focusing on joint degree programmes, doctoral research and ship-design studies.
The Letters of Collaboration (LoCs) were exchanged between Universiti Kuala Lumpur (UniKL) and Universiti Poly-Tech Malaysia (UPTM) with Sabancı University and Yildiz Technical University (YTU) here.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, Mara chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki and newly-appointed Deputy Director-General (Education) Shahrizal Mohd Saderi witnessed the exchange.
Asyraf said the collaborations were among the key initiatives Zahid had driven after Türkiye's Council of Higher Education president Prof Dr Erol Özvar visited Malaysia in April.
"Among the main focuses of this collaboration is research exchange and, most importantly, for Malaysian students to come and study here and for their students to come to our country.
"What we have proposed is a double degree, where students who secure a place at UniKL and UPTM, for example, will at the same time have the chance to study at universities in Türkiye, gaining two degrees at once," he said at a press conference today following the LoCs exchange.
Asyraf said this would also give those in Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) fields wider pathways to careers and higher education, including studying abroad, particularly in Türkiye.
Under the proposed collaboration with Sabancı University, both institutions will explore joint bachelor's and master's degree programmes, including curriculum mapping and academic delivery arrangements.
The partnership will also explore doctoral co-education pathways, involving joint supervision and collaborative research.
Meanwhile, the proposed collaboration with YTU will focus on joint ship-design research and model testing, leveraging the complementary facilities available at both universities.
YTU's wave-tank facilities will support shallow-water studies, while UniKL's Malaysian Institute of Marine Engineering Technology will contribute its facilities for deep-water studies.

Title: Nothing to hide: Umno welcomes audit of Najib crowdfunding, says Asyraf
Article:
ISTANBUL: Umno has nothing to hide and welcomes any audit of its RM50 million crowdfunding effort for former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, said its secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki.
He said the party had been transparent from the start, with a separate account established for the Najib Razak Solidarity Fund following an Umno Supreme Council decision.
"When we decided on the special fund, we set aside a separate account for this.
"We did this in a transparent manner. If they want to audit, we are open and welcome it because there is nothing to hide," he said.
Asyraf said the fund came from a crowdfunding effort and all the money came from the public.
He dismissed claims that some of it came from "towkay" who received projects from the Rural and Regional Development Ministry.
He described the claims as "slander".
He said people had donated as little as RM20, and that he monitored the account online each hour to ensure that all donations went into it.
"Nothing went through any other account or any individual," he said.
Asyraf was responding to a call by former Damansara member of parliament
Tony Pua
for Bank Negara Malaysia and the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) to audit the fund.
Pua said an audit was necessary to ensure that the money raised was legitimate and had not been laundered.
Umno settled Najib's
RM50 million
fine through the Najib Razak Solidarity Fund, which was launched in September.
Najib has been in Kajang Prison since Aug 23, 2022, after being convicted of misappropriating RM42 million belonging to SRC International Sdn Bhd.
He was sentenced to 12 years' jail and fined RM210 million, which the
Federal Territories Pardons Board
reduced in January 2024 to six years and RM50 million.
On Sept 18, Najib was granted a further conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.
This was subject to payment of the RM50 million fine and compliance with other conditions.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar extends Deepavali greetings, calls for stronger national unity
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Deepavali celebration should serve as a platform to strengthen unity, bridge gaps between communities and foster values of compassion and concern for those in need.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said that in a multiracial society rooted in diverse cultures and traditions, the values of mutual respect, understanding and the acceptance of differences must continue to be reinforced.
"May this Deepavali inspire a renewed spirit to foster a more open, noble and progressive mindset, thereby elevating the dignity of the people and strengthening the nation's harmony," he said in a Facebook post today.
Anwar also extended his Deepavali greetings to all those celebrating the festival, expressing his hope that it brings happiness, peace and prosperity.
"Deepavali arrives bearing a ray of joy, enlivening the spirit of the 'Festival of Lights', which symbolises the triumph of light over darkness, the victory of goodness over evil, and the power of knowledge to liberate humanity from the shackles of ignorance and arrogance.
"
Deepavali Nalvaalthukkal
! (Deepavali greetings)," he added. – BERNAMA
