Title: Asyraf: No need for A-G to meet King over Najib's house arrest
Article:
ISTANBUL: There is no need for the Attorney-General to be told to meet Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, to explain legal issues surrounding Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest, says an Umno leader.
The party's secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the King's power to grant pardons was clearly enshrined in the Federal Constitution. This includes reducing sentences.
"So when the King has decreed through the proper process, namely through the Pardons Board, the decision cannot be disputed.
"So there is no need for the Attorney-General to be directed to meet the King to explain," he said when met here.
Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar is
seeking an audience
with Sultan Ibrahim to explain his position on complying with the royal decree concerning Najib's conditional pardon.
The Prime Minister's Office said Dusuki would also explain legal questions arising from the High Court's discharge order following payment of the RM50 million fine, a condition for the house arrest.
It said the court needed to determine these issues as they affected the commencement date of Najib's prison sentence in the 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) case.
Najib was convicted of misappropriating RM42 million in SRC International funds and began serving his 12-year prison sentence at Kajang Prison on Aug 23, 2022.
In 2024, his jail term was halved to six years and his fine reduced from RM210 million to RM50 million.
On Sept 18, Sultan Ibrahim granted Najib a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine.
Najib's lawyers paid the fine yesterday. The Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) later called for the implementation of the house arrest to be temporarily deferred pending judicial clarification on the legal effect of the High Court's discharge order.
Istana Negara today said the conditional pardon granted to Najib on Sept 18 was clear, explicit and unambiguous, and unrelated to any other cases involving him.
The palace said all conditions imposed under the pardon had been fulfilled, warning that any attempt to dispute the order would amount to
defying the King's decree
.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: King's decree already answered A-GC's questions, says Najib's lawyers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The decree by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia on Datuk Seri Najib Razak's conditional pardon had already addressed all questions raised by the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC), his lawyers said.
In a statement, Messrs Shafee & Co, representing the former prime minister, said the decree issued through Istana Negara today had made clear that the Conditional Pardon Order dated Sept 18 was issued by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution.
They said His Majesty had specifically emphasised that the order was "clear, explicit and unambiguous", was not connected to any other cases involving Najib, and that all its conditions had been fulfilled.
The lawyers also noted that the Pardons Board meeting at which the advice on the order was presented to the King had been attended by the Attorney-General himself.
They said the King's decree had also stressed that there should be no confusion over the order's interpretation or prolonged uncertainty over its implementation.
Shafee & Co said the A-GC could not rely on the High Court's Order of Discharge on Payment of Fine, issued on Friday following Najib's payment of the RM50 million fine, to alter the terms of the royal decree.
The lawyers argued that the court order must be read in its entirety, including its title and recital confirming that the fine had been paid.
They said payment of the fine discharged Najib's liability to pay it but did not, by itself, terminate his prison sentence.
They also said that the same court order recorded that Najib was to serve his sentence under house arrest in accordance with the Pardon Order, which they said had been acknowledged by the A-GC on Friday.
The lawyers maintained that the conditional pardon was an exercise of the King's prerogative under Article 42, adding that neither the courts nor the Attorney-General could reopen the manner in which the King had exercised that power after receiving the Pardons Board's advice.
They argued that the High Court order implementing the pardon after recording payment of the RM50 million fine could not change the terms of the King's decree.
On the A-GC's latest response, Shafee & Co said the former had issued another media statement at 12.42pm today, 57 minutes after the King's decree, but had made no reference to it.
They said the A-GC had also neither withdrawn its Nov 6 statement announcing a temporary suspension of the house arrest arrangement nor confirmed that the suspension had been lifted.
Earlier, the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) said the
Attorney-General had sought an audience
with His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, to explain his position on the matter.
The PMO said Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar would also explain legal questions arising from the High Court's release order following payment of the RM50 million fine, which was a condition for Najib's house arrest.
It said the issues must be determined by the court as they have implications for the commencement date of Najib's prison sentence in the 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) case.
Istana Negara today said
the conditional pardon granted to Najib on Sept 18 was clear, explicit and unambiguous, and unrelated to any other cases involving him.
The palace said all conditions imposed under the pardon had been fulfilled, warning that any attempt to dispute the order would amount to defying the King's decree.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Ab Rauf's track record offers confidence in BN-PN manifesto delivery
Article:
MELAKA: The Barisan Nasional-Perikatan Nasional (BN-PN) joint manifesto provides a comprehensive roadmap for Melaka's development, with a focus on economic opportunities and public welfare, say political analysts.
They said the
113 initiatives
outlined in the manifesto addressed key concerns affecting the people, including the cost of living, affordable housing, employment opportunities and economic growth.
Political analyst Dr Mohammad Tawfik Yaakub said the proposals, which include free water, affordable housing, employment opportunities and a RM30 billion investment target, reflected an effort to address the needs of different segments of society.
He said the continuation and expansion of existing policies could also provide an opportunity to build on programmes that had already benefited the community.
"Their implementation will depend on financial resources, administrative capacity and clear timelines.
"The key consideration is whether these commitments can translate into measurable improvements in people's daily lives," he said.
[[nid:1572990]]
Tawfik said the ability of BN and PN to maintain political consensus would be important in ensuring the smooth implementation of the manifesto if they formed the next state government.
He said the experience of both coalitions in negotiating seat allocations highlighted the importance of having clear decision-making mechanisms, particularly in matters involving executive responsibilities and resource allocation.
"Both coalitions must establish a clear decision-making mechanism to prevent political differences from delaying development programmes or affecting administrative efficiency," he said.
He said Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh's experience working with Pakatan Harapan demonstrated his ability to foster cooperation among parties with differing political interests.
"Leadership experience is relevant, but long-term stability also depends on the willingness of coalition partners to resolve disagreements constructively," he said.
[[nid:1572989]]
On the manifesto's inclusivity, Tawfik said its initiatives should benefit all communities through fair access to development opportunities, public services and welfare programmes.
He said transparent eligibility criteria, inclusive representation and consistent engagement with urban and rural populations would be essential in ensuring that no community was left behind.
Meanwhile, Universiti Teknologi Mara Faculty of Communication and Media Studies senior lecturer Dr Siti Faidul Maisarah Abdullah described the joint manifesto as people-friendly, with initiatives aimed at improving the welfare and living standards of Melaka residents.
Siti Faidul said Ab Rauf's leadership experience, including his previous cooperation with PH, reflected his ability to navigate different political arrangements and work with parties across the political divide.
She said his administration's reported achievement of fulfilling 97 per cent of its previous manifesto pledges could also strengthen public confidence in the latest commitments.
She acknowledged that differences in political approaches and grassroots structures between BN and PN would require both coalitions to work towards a common understanding in managing a joint administration.
[[nid:1572988]]
"Although they are two different political entities, their objective remains the same, which is to ensure that people can live in peace and harmony.
"Mature discussions and fair solutions are needed to navigate the challenges of this new political landscape," she said.
Siti Faidul added that the partnership should continue prioritising the interests of all communities, regardless of race, religion or political affiliation.
She said Ab Rauf's track record and the cooperation between BN and PN could provide continuity in the state's development, with the ultimate measure of the partnership being its ability to deliver on the commitments made to the people.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BN-PN must ensure vote transfer to secure Melaka victory, says KJ
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: The success of the electoral cooperation between Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional in the Melaka election will depend on whether supporters of both coalitions are willing to transfer their votes to each other's candidates.
Former Umno Youth chief Khairy Jamaluddin said the arrangement would translate into electoral success only if grassroots supporters were prepared to back candidates from allied parties, even when their preferred party was not contesting.
He said the Melaka election would serve as an important test of whether the cooperation could deliver another electoral victory, following the formula adopted in the recent Negri Sembilan election.
"There is no point having a strategy and political cooperation if there is no transfer of votes.
"If voters do not see a candidate from the party they support, but there is a candidate from a cooperating party, they should give their vote to that candidate.
"That is what we are appealing for — a transfer of votes between supporters of the cooperating parties," he told reporters while campaigning for BN candidate for Rembia, Azril Aziz, here today.
Khairy said the arrangement required Pas and PN supporters to back BN candidates in constituencies where their parties were not contesting, and vice versa.
"Here in Rembia, those who previously supported Pas or PN should support the BN candidate because their parties are not contesting here.
"If this formula worked in Negri Sembilan, it will also be accepted in Melaka," he said.
Khairy said the outcome could also provide an early indication of how similar political cooperation might play out in the next general election.
"This could once again serve as a precursor to what might happen in the coming general election," he said.
Meanwhile, Khairy said BN's campaign strategy also focused on fielding candidates who were familiar with their constituencies and had established relationships with local communities.
He said Azril was among those who fitted the approach, having served in various positions within Umno and the local administration.
"Azril has extensive experience as a long-time Umno activist, having served as a division secretary, a Youth leader and a special officer at the state constituency development and coordination committee (Japerun).
"He knows the people here, and they know him. He also understands the workings of local administration and the responsibilities of an elected representative," he said.
Khairy said BN's advantage in the election also stemmed from the performance of the Melaka government under caretaker Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Najib's lawyers want ex-PM transferred to Langgak Duta tonight
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Najib Razak's lawyers have called on the Commissioner-General of Prisons to transfer the former prime minister to his Jalan Langgak Duta residence tonight, in line with the King's decree.
Messrs Shafee & Co also urged the Attorney-General's Chambers to immediately withdraw the "temporary deferment" of Najib's house arrest.
"His Majesty's order must be implemented today," the firm said in a statement.
The lawyers said there should be no confusion over the interpretation of the pardon or prolonged uncertainty over its implementation.
"The pardon is clear and expressed without any ambiguity, and not connected to any other case against him.
"All conditions of the pardon have been met, and any argument disputing the order tends towards defying the order of His Majesty."
Earlier, the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) said the
Attorney-General had sought an audience with His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia
, to explain his position on the matter.
The PMO said Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar would also explain legal questions arising from the High Court's release order following payment of the RM50 million fine, which was a condition for Najib's house arrest.
It said the issues must be determined by the court as they have implications for the commencement date of Najib's prison sentence in the 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) case.
Istana Negara today said
the conditional pardon granted to Najib on Sept 18 was clear, explicit and unambiguous, and unrelated to any other cases involving him.
The palace said all conditions imposed under the pardon had been fulfilled, warning that any attempt to dispute the order would amount to defying the King's decree.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid: There should be no "delaying tactics" in implementing Najib's house arrest
Article:
ISTANBUL: Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said there should be no "delaying tactics" to stall the implementation of Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest following the payment of the RM50 million fine.
He said Umno stood by the decision of the  Pardons Board, which was chaired by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, adding that it was the King's absolute authority under the Federal Constitution.
Zahid said the matter must be complied with by all parties, including the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC).
"Although some parties have questioned the crowdfunding that Umno worked on for a certain period, it was a joint effort on our part.
"Once that has been fulfilled (the fine), there should be no delaying tactics to put off the Pardons Board's decision.
"To me, what has been decided is crystal clear and must be obeyed, including by the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC)," he told a press conference here.
Zahid said Umno did not wish to question the powers of any department or office holder but believed the order issued must be obeyed.
"We also do not want to see any contradiction with earlier statements issued by the A-GC on Najib's case," he said.
Yesterday, Umno confirmed that the
RM50 million
fine imposed on Najib had been paid at the Kuala Lumpur High Court, paving the way for the implementation of house arrest under the terms of his conditional pardon.
On Sept 18, the Federal Territories Pardons Board announced that His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, had consented to a conditional pardon at the board's 64th meeting.
His Majesty allowed Najib to serve the remainder of his six-year sentence under house arrest, subject to payment of the
RM50 million
SRC International fine.
The board said Najib must comply with all conditions imposed for him to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.
Najib has been serving a reduced six-year prison sentence at Kajang Prison after the board halved his original 12-year sentence in February 2024.
The initial RM210 million fine was also reduced to RM50 million.
Najib is serving the sentence after the Federal Court upheld his conviction in the SRC International corruption case on Aug 23, 2022.
He was found guilty of seven charges involving abuse of power, criminal breach of trust and money laundering over RM42 million belonging to SRC International, a former unit of 1Malaysia Development Bhd. He was sentenced to 12 years' jail and fined RM210 million.
He was taken to Kajang Prison the same day to begin serving his sentence, making him the first former prime minister to be imprisoned following a criminal conviction.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: King's prerogative to pardon Najib cannot be questioned, says Anwar
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the prerogative of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, to grant a conditional pardon to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak could not be questioned.
He said the decision on Najib's pardon in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case was based on the King's decree, with all preparations for its implementation already carried out.
"The question arising now is the second case (1MDB), whether it can be implemented or not. That case will be finalised by the Attorney-General and the judiciary," he said.
Speaking on the sidelines of the 2026 National Family Month celebration, Anwar said he had asked the Attorney-General to seek an audience with the King to explain the matter.
Earlier today,
Istana Negara said
the conditional pardon granted to Najib on Sept 18 was clear, explicit and unambiguous, and unrelated to any other cases involving him.
The palace said all conditions imposed under the pardon had been fulfilled, warning that any attempt to dispute the order would amount to defying the King's decree.
The pardon allows Najib to serve the remainder of his SRC International prison sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of a RM50 million fine.
The fine was paid in full at the Kuala Lumpur High Court yesterday.
However, the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) later
proposed temporarily deferring the house arrest
arrangement pending judicial clarification on the legal effect of the High Court's discharge order.
Anwar said a few days might be needed to obtain clarification and determine the legal position.
"That is not under my jurisdiction as prime minister.
"However, the decree of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong has been decided and we, as citizens, must obey, respect and understand the meaning of the Constitution and the jurisdiction of the King," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: A-G seeking audience with Sultan Ibrahim to explain Najib house arrest issue
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Attorney-General has sought an audience with His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, to express his position on complying with the royal decree on the Conditional Pardon Order granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
The Prime Minister's Office, in a statement, said the A-G, Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar, will also explain the legal questions arising from the High Court's Release Order following the payment of the RM50 million fine, which was a precondition for Najib's house arrest.
According to the statement, the issues must be determined by the court as they have implications for the commencement date of the prison sentence in Najib's 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) case.
Najib was convicted of misappropriating RM42 million in SRC International funds and began serving his 12-year prison sentence at Kajang Prison on Aug 23, 2022.
On Jan 29, 2024, the Pardons Board agreed to halve his sentence to six years and reduce his fine from RM210 million to RM50 million.
At the 64th meeting of the Federal Territories Pardons Board on Sept 18, 2026, Sultan Ibrahim granted Najib a new conditional pardon, allowing him to serve the remainder of his SRC International prison sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028.
This was subject to him paying the outstanding RM50 million fine.
On Friday, it was reported that Najib was making arrangements to be transferred out of Kajang Prison after his lawyers made the RM50 million payment at the Kuala Lumpur High Court.
However, the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC), in a statement, disputed the validity of Najib's conditional pardon and said the execution of the house arrest should be deferred.
Istana Negara today issued a statement addressing the matter and reaffirming the constitutional authority of the King in granting pardons.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today asked Dusuki to seek an audience with Sultan Ibrahim to explain the legal issues surrounding the matter, including its implications for Najib's 1MDB case.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: A-G should take leave over Najib house arrest issue, says KJ
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar should take immediate leave pending police investigations into reports lodged against him over the issue surrounding Datuk Seri Najib Razak's conditional pardon, Khairy Jamaluddin said.
The former Umno Youth chief said the Attorney-General should temporarily step aside to ensure transparency and integrity in the investigation, particularly as any findings by the police could eventually be referred to the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC).
"The Attorney-General must take leave. He is now the subject of an investigation following the police reports lodged against him.
"When police reports are lodged, investigations must be carried out. If the investigations establish a case, the findings must be referred to the A-GC.
"But the head of the A-GC is the Attorney-General himself, who is now the subject of the investigation," he told reporters while campaigning for Barisan Nasional candidate for Rembia, Azril Aziz.
Khairy said his call was not for Dusuki to be dismissed, adding that such a decision was the prerogative of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, acting on the advice of the Prime Minister.
"I am asking the Attorney-General to take temporary leave. I am not calling for his dismissal.
"Given the statement he issued and the subsequent response from Istana Negara, which I consider very serious, this has now resulted in police reports being lodged."
Khairy said several police reports had been lodged against Dusuki, including by
Umno Youth
.
Yesterday, the A-GC issued a statement disputing the validity of Najib's conditional pardon.
Istana Negara today issued a statement addressing the matter and reaffirming the constitutional authority of the King in granting pardons.
The A-GC's position drew criticism following the royal statement.
Khairy also questioned the timing of the Attorney-General's statement, noting that several weeks had passed since the decision on Najib's conditional pardon.
He said the statement was issued only after Najib had fulfilled the RM50 million payment condition stipulated in the pardon.
"There was a considerable gap of several weeks between the decision and the Attorney-General's statement yesterday. The statement was suddenly issued only after the RM50 million payment condition had been fulfilled.
"That is why several police reports have been lodged."
It was reported that Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had asked Dusuki to
seek an audience
with His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, over Najib's house arrest.
Anwar said Dusuki should explain the legal issues surrounding the matter, including its implications for Najib's 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) case.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Respect King's powers to grant pardons, says Wee Ka Siong
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Those who claim to respect the royal institution and constitution cannot act in ways that contradict those principles, says MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong.
Wee said this in calling for the King's powers to grant pardons to be respected.
He said there should be no contradictions of the decisions made by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, concerning former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest.
"We cannot, on the one hand, proclaim our respect for the royal institution and our commitment to defending the Constitution, while on the other hand, act in ways that contradict those very principles," he said in a statement.
He said any legal questions surrounding Najib's house arrest should be resolved swiftly through the proper channels rather than used as grounds for delaying its implementation.
The Attorney-General's Chambers said today that seeking a court ruling on Najib's house arrest did not override the King's power to grant pardons.
It said the King's constitutional authority to grant pardons and the courts' power to interpret the legal effect of an order were separate matters.
Wee said respect for the rule of law and respect for the constitutional authority of the Ruler were not mutually exclusive.
"True respect is not measured by how loudly we proclaim our loyalty, but by whether our actions consistently uphold the constitutional authority of His Majesty and the dignity of our constitutional monarchy," he said.
Yesterday, Umno paid Najib's RM50 million fine at the Kuala Lumpur High Court, fulfilling a condition of the royal pardon granted by Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim on Sept 18.
The pardon allows Najib to serve the remainder of his SRC International prison sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to compliance with stipulated conditions.
However, the
A-GC
subsequently called for the implementation of house arrest to be temporarily deferred pending clarification of legal questions surrounding the pardon and the effect of the High Court's orders.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid receives courtesy call from Malaysian Honorary Consul in Bursa
Article:
ISTANBUL: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today received a courtesy call from Malaysia's Honorary Consul in Bursa, Turkiye, Datuk Cevdet Sefer.
The 30-minute meeting began at 11am (4pm Malaysian time) at Zahid's hotel here.
Zahid highlighted opportunities for Turkish investors and companies to expand into Malaysia, positioning the country as a strategic gateway to the wider Asean market.
He also proposed exploring commercially viable joint ventures in renewable energy, recycling and sustainable industrial development, with an emphasis on technology transfer and Malaysian participation.
Zahid, who is also the National Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) Council chairman, welcomed cooperation in TVET that combines investment with industrial attachments, technical training and skills transfer for Malaysian youth and workers.
Zahid also discussed the development of the Malaysian Institute of Marine Engineering Technology in Lumut, Perak.
He asked Sefer to identify realistic investment or trade opportunities for follow-up with the relevant agencies in Malaysia.
Zahid also discussed the need to translate the Malaysia-Türkiye Comprehensive Strategic Partnership into concrete business opportunities, quality jobs and mutually beneficial investments.
The deputy prime minister is in Turkiye for a four-day working visit in conjunction with the 2026 TRT World Forum.
Yesterday, he attended the forum's opening ceremony, officiated by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan at the Istanbul Congress Centre, before taking part in a session titled "Türkiye: From Regional Power to Multi-Regional Actor".
The two-day forum, which began yesterday, is themed "A World Without a Center: Who Leads When the Rules Run Out?" and brings together political leaders, policymakers, academics, media practitioners and civil society representatives from around the world.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mak Yong, Wayang Kulit master Che Mat named Living National Heritage
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Nearly six decades of dedication to preserving Kelantan's Mak Yong and Wayang Kulit traditions have earned Che Mat Jusoh, an Adiguru (master practitioner) of traditional performing arts at Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM), recognition as a Living National Heritage (WAKOH) figure for 2026.
In a statement today, USM said the prestigious honour was conferred by the National Heritage Department under the Tourism, Arts and Culture Ministry in appreciation of his longstanding efforts to safeguard the traditional art forms, which are an integral part of the nation's cultural heritage.
The university said the recognition was conferred during the 6th National Heritage Declaration Ceremony, held recently at the ministry, where 39 heritage elements were also officially declared National Heritage.
Che Mat, 72, said the award was more than a personal honour, describing it as an acknowledgement of his efforts to preserve traditional art forms that are increasingly being marginalised.
He expressed delight that his longstanding dedication to safeguarding these traditions had finally earned recognition from the government.
Che Mat said he was among the few remaining practitioners capable of performing traditional Mak Yong musical pieces that were gradually being forgotten, but was encouraged by the growing interest among younger generations in learning the traditional art forms.
"However, passing down knowledge of traditional arts takes time, patience and commitment. It is a gradual process that cannot be rushed, just as I experienced during my own years of learning," he said in the same statement.
Che Mat expressed hope that traditional arts and cultural heritage would continue to be preserved and strengthened for future generations, while encouraging young people to broaden their appreciation beyond singing, acting and dancing to include writing on arts and culture.
He also stressed the importance of documentation and writing in safeguarding the knowledge, history and philosophy of traditional heritage, ensuring they are preserved for future generations.
Beyond his involvement in traditional performing arts, Che Mat, a former visiting artist at USM, has also contributed to literature with the publication of his latest book, Hikayat Maharaja Seri Rama, this year.
Compiled by Che Mat and published by Nusa Centre with financial support from the ministry, the book aims to document the rich Malay literary heritage that has flourished across the Malay Archipelago for more than 1,000 years.
The recognition also underscores the vital role of traditional arts practitioners in documenting, safeguarding and passing down the nation's cultural knowledge, skills and intangible heritage to future generations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid, Lebanese deputy PM discuss post-conflict reconstruction
Article:
ISTANBUL: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi yesterday received courtesy calls from his Lebanese counterpart Dr Tarek Mitri and the Developing Eight (D-8) Organisation for Economic Cooperation secretary-general Sohail Mahmood.
Zahid said his discussion with Mitri focused on security developments in Lebanon and post-conflict recovery efforts to help its people rebuild their lives.
"We also discussed potential cooperation in infrastructure reconstruction and community economic development, humanitarian assistance, technical and vocational education and training, as well as defence to strengthen Lebanon's capabilities and resilience," he said in a statement.
The courtesy calls took place on the sidelines of the 2026 TRT World Forum at the Istanbul Congress Centre.
Zahid said Malaysia and Lebanon share close, friendly ties, particularly through the deployment of the Malaysian Battalion (Malbatt) under the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon since 2007.
He said the contribution of Malaysian peacekeepers reflected the country's continued commitment to peace and stability in southern Lebanon.
"I believe the commitment between both countries should extend beyond peacekeeping operations through cooperation that provides moral support and creates economic opportunities for the well-being of the Lebanese people," he said.
On the meeting with Sohail, Zahid said they exchanged views on the grouping's role in strengthening economic cooperation amid global challenges affecting its member states.
He said Malaysia saw the importance of continuing to use the D-8 platform to strengthen ties among friendly nations, widen cooperation and build collective economic resilience.
The D-8 was established in 1997 to enhance economic cooperation among developing countries. Its members are Malaysia, Indonesia, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Iran, Turkiye, Egypt and Nigeria.
Zahid said both meetings reflected Malaysia's commitment to active and constructive international engagement.
"Malaysia will continue to prioritise dialogue, understanding and practical cooperation in supporting peace and shared prosperity," he said.
Zahid is in Türkiye for a four-day working visit in conjunction with the 2026 TRT World Forum.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PM congratulates Kedah's top STA 2026 school SMA Nahdhah Hasanah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated Sekolah Menengah Agama Nahdhah Hasanah in Melele, Kodiang, after it emerged as the top-performing school in Kedah in the 2026 Sijil Tinggi Agama (STA) examination.
In a post on X today, Anwar said the school's achievement was undoubtedly underpinned by the exceptional dedication of its teachers and the sacrifices of parents.
"I share in the joy of the great achievement of the students of SMA Nahdhah Hasanah. This success is certainly driven by the extraordinary guidance of teachers and the sacrifices of parents. May they continue to excel, Insya-Allah," he said.
SMA Nahdhah Hasanah, which has been in operation since 1946, was visited by the prime minister on June 17, 2023, in conjunction with the school's diamond jubilee celebration.
In the 2026 STA, the school recorded a School Average Grade (GPS) of 2.79, with 100 per cent of its students qualifying for the certificate.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid, Erdoğan discuss lifting Malaysia–Turkiye trade to US$10 billion by 2030
Article:
ISTANBUL: Malaysia–Turkiye strategic ties must go beyond traditional cooperation and translate into concrete initiatives, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said.
Zahid said this after a 30-minute meeting with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan on the sidelines of the 2026 TRT World Forum here yesterday.
"We exchanged views on the need to widen economic and trade relations between our two countries, particularly to raise bilateral trade from US$5.6 billion in 2025 to US$10 billion by 2030.
"As such, the High-Level Strategic Cooperation Council, which held its first meeting in Ankara in January, is an important mechanism for coordinating priorities.
"It also speeds up the implementation of Malaysia–Turkiye strategic cooperation, in line with the countries' Comprehensive Strategic Partnership," he said in a statement.
Zahid said he also outlined potential areas for cooperation, including investment, the defence industry, technology transfer, technical and vocational education and training (TVET), the halal industry and disaster management.
He said the strategic relationship should be translated into initiatives that open up investment opportunities, strengthen industrial capacity, expand the transfer of expertise and improve the economic competitiveness of both countries.
On Asean–Turkiye relations, Zahid, as country coordinator, reaffirmed Malaysia's commitment to strengthening ties between the two, focusing on trade expansion, technology cooperation and human capital development.
He said that Malaysia would continue to pursue constructive, principled diplomacy rooted in national interest, while deepening cooperation with international partners.
He said participation in international forums such as the 2026 TRT World Forum gives Malaysia room to share perspectives, voice the country's position and strengthen networks with international leaders and policymakers.
"Malaysia will continue to adopt a diplomatic approach that is constructive, principled and anchored in the national interest, while strengthening cooperation with international partners to contribute to peace, stability and prosperity for all," he said.
Zahid is in Turkiye for a four-day working visit at the invitation of the 2026 TRT World Forum to attend the forum.
He also took part in a panel session titled "Türkiye: From Regional Power to Multi-Regional Actor".
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: More than new clothes and sweets, Deepavali is about family and tradition
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 7 — Deepavali celebrations are not just about wearing new attire and preparing an array of traditional delicacies, but also about strengthening family bonds and preserving age-old traditions passed down through generations.
For Singaporean P. Parvathy, 65, from Sengkang, a visit to Johor Bahru to shop for Deepavali essentials has become an annual tradition, while also giving her the opportunity to meet relatives living in the state.
She said her visit to the Deepavali Bazaar at Jalan Ungku Puan here also allowed her to browse a variety of decorative items for the home, including floral ornaments to hang at the entrance, traditional attire and bangles.
“I came to buy flowers to hang at the door. After this, I also want to buy clothes and bangles. This year, I find that the items on sale are even more beautiful than before,” she told Bernama recently.
Sharing how Deepavali is celebrated in Singapore, Parvathy said preparations at her home begin on the eve of the festival, with various delicacies prepared to be enjoyed with family members and guests.
She said that on Deepavali morning, the entire family would wake up as early as 5am to bathe, perform prayers and enjoy a traditional breakfast such as thosai before welcoming visits from relatives and friends.
She said the practice of gathering and sharing meals remained one of the traditions that continued to add to the festive atmosphere of her family’s Deepavali celebrations each year.
Little India in Brickfields bustles with activity as shoppers make a last-minute dash for Deepavali essentials. — Bernama pic
Meanwhile, for housewife K. Kalaivani, 40, from Pasir Gudang, this year’s Deepavali holds special significance as her family will also be holding a religious ceremony to mark her daughter’s coming of age.
The mother of four said that apart from preparing traditional attire, including saris, for her family members, she had also bought flowers for the religious ceremony and several other necessities.
She said the preparations were not only for the Deepavali celebrations but also to mark a meaningful occasion for her family in conjunction with her daughter’s religious ceremony.
Meanwhile, traditional snack seller Renuka, 34, who wished to be identified only by her first name, is offering more than 50 varieties of biscuits and savoury snacks in conjunction with Deepavali, giving the Indian community a wide selection to complete their festive spread.
She said sales, which began more than 15 days before Deepavali, allowed customers to choose from a variety of snacks to serve to family members, relatives and guests visiting their homes.
Among the items available are tarts, suji and murukku, priced from RM35 per jar, while customers can purchase four jars at a promotional price of RM120.
She said the variety of snacks also complemented the tradition of visiting family and friends, which adds to the festive atmosphere of Deepavali celebrations each year.
Deepavali, also known as the Festival of Lights, will be celebrated tomorrow by Hindus across the country. — Bernama

Title: This Deepavali, Anwar calls on Malaysians to celebrate differences and shared values
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — The Deepavali celebration should serve as a platform to strengthen unity, bridge gaps between communities and foster values of compassion and concern for those in need.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said that in a multiracial society rooted in diverse cultures and traditions, the values of mutual respect, understanding and the acceptance of differences must continue to be reinforced.
“May this Deepavali inspire a renewed spirit to foster a more open, noble and progressive mindset, thereby elevating the dignity of the people and strengthening the nation’s harmony,” he said in a Facebook post today.
Anwar also extended his Deepavali greetings to all those celebrating the festival, expressing his hope that it brings happiness, peace and prosperity.
“Deepavali arrives bearing a ray of joy, enlivening the spirit of the ‘Festival of Lights’, which symbolises the triumph of light over darkness, the victory of goodness over evil, and the power of knowledge to liberate humanity from the shackles of ignorance and arrogance.
“
Deepavali Nalvaalthukkal
! (Deepavali greetings),” he added. — Bernama

Title: After deadly Paya Terubong landslide, Chow says DOSH must finish probe first
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 7 — The Penang state government will decide whether to set up a State Commission of Inquiry (SCI) into the Taman Seri Rambai landslide in Paya Terubong once the state Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH) completes its investigation and submits its findings and recommendations.
Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the state government would await the findings of the DOSH investigation before considering further action over the incident, which claimed the life of a 73-year-old doctor.
He said he had yet to receive any updates on the progress of the investigation.
“DOSH is conducting its investigation and will provide recommendations (to the state government) once it is completed. A decision on whether to establish an SCI will only be made after that,” he told reporters after officiating at the Penang AI Future Makers Bootcamp 2026 at SEGi College Penang here today.
He was responding to calls from several quarters for the state government to establish an SCI to conduct an independent investigation into the Oct 25 landslide tragedy.
When asked whether residents affected by the landslide could return to their homes, Chow said the matter had yet to be determined as the area had not been declared safe.
Earlier, several state assemblymen and non-governmental organisations (NGOs) had called for an independent investigation into the fatal landslide and demanded action against those responsible for the hillside development.
In the 8.36 am incident, Dr Wong Kar Lin was killed after being buried in a landslide that struck his home, while his wife, Chang Mei Nuo, 68, and mother-in-law, Wong Poh Lim, who is in her 80s, managed to escape. — Bernama

Title: Zahid says Malaysia stands ready to help Lebanon rebuild after conflict
Article:
ISTANBUL, Nov 7 — Malaysia is ready to help Lebanon rebuild following the conflict that has affected the country, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said.
He said this could include rebuilding infrastructure and local economies, providing humanitarian assistance, offering Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), and strengthening defence cooperation to enhance Lebanon’s capabilities and resilience.
“Malaysia and Lebanon share a special friendship, particularly through Malaysia’s involvement in peacekeeping operations under the Malaysian Battalion (MALBATT) since 2007.
“For nearly two decades, our peacekeepers have played an important role in supporting peace and stability in southern Lebanon,” he said here today.
Ahmad Zahid, who is currently in Turkiye for a four-day working visit from Nov 5 to 8 in conjunction with his participation in the TRT World Forum 2026, said he believed Malaysia’s commitment to Lebanon would continue beyond the end of the MALBATT peacekeeping mission in January 2027, following the termination of the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) mandate at the end of this year.
He said the friendship between the two countries should instead continue through cooperation to help Lebanese rebuild their lives, regain hope for the future and achieve lasting peace.
“Peace is not simply the end of war, but the beginning of efforts to rebuild lives,” he said.
Ahmad Zahid, who also serves as Rural and Regional Development Minister, earlier met with Lebanese Deputy Prime Minister Dr Tarek Mitri after the TRT World Forum 2026 at the Istanbul Congress Centre (ICC) yesterday.
Ahmad Zahid also met Developing Eight (D-8) Secretary-General Sohail Mahmood to exchange views on ways to enhance cooperation among member states, particularly in tackling economic challenges and global geopolitical uncertainties.
He said the talks also explored the potential of a market comprising more than 1.2 billion people, noting that D-8 had considerable scope to expand trade, investment and strategic ties among member states.
“I also highlighted opportunities for cooperation in the halal industry, TVET, food security and the development of small and medium enterprises, including expanding economic opportunities for rural communities.
“I believe the strength of D-8 lies not merely in the size of its market, but in its member countries’ ability to translate cooperation into shared prosperity. Malaysia will remain committed to playing an active role in ensuring that this potential is harnessed for the benefit of its people. Insya-Allah,” he said.
Established in 1997, D-8 aims to promote economic cooperation among eight developing countries: Malaysia, Indonesia, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Iran, Turkiye, Egypt and Nigeria.
Ahmad Zahid said both meetings reflected Malaysia’s commitment to active and constructive international engagement, with continued emphasis on dialogue, mutual understanding and practical cooperation in support of peace and shared prosperity. — Bernama

Title: Penang sets aside RM4.5m to grow startups, AI adoption and digital economy
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 7 — The Penang government has allocated RM4.5 million in its 2027 budget to support technology startups, accelerate digitalisation among small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and expand the use of artificial intelligence (AI) across the state’s economy.
Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the allocation is to strengthen the state’s technology start-up ecosystem and help businesses embrace digital transformation.
“In (the state’s) Budget 2027, the state government has set aside RM4.5 million for Digital Penang; it will support technology start-ups, help small and medium enterprises go digital, and use AI across our economy. The startup community supported by the initiative has already generated 310 companies and created approximately 1,720 jobs,” he said when officiating the AI Future Makers Bootcamp 2026 at SEGi College Penang here today.
Also present at the AI Future Makers Bootcamp 2026 were chairman Lukas J.Tan and SEGi College Penang head of student experience Vincent Tung Chin Aun.
Chow said the collaboration between young innovators and experienced industry players demonstrated the importance of learning across generations as Penang prepared its workforce for technological changes. He noted that the state had successfully adapted to previous industrial transformations, including when the country’s first Free Trade Zone was established in Bayan Lepas in 1972, with workers acquiring new skills through on-the-job training and knowledge-sharing.
“Penang knows how to do this. When the world changed, we learned fast, and we learned together. The world is changing again,” he added, noting that AI could now complete in an afternoon tasks that previously took a week.
On talent development, Chow said 675 fresh graduates and working professionals had undergone chip design training through the Penang Chip Design Academy, with 85 per cent of them securing employment. He said the Penang Talent Focus Group, launched in June under the Penang Workplace initiative, also brought together industry players, universities and human resource practitioners to improve the matching of talent with employment opportunities.
Meanwhile, the Penang Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) Blueprint will also introduce AI learning programmes to rural schools through mobile initiatives.
The chief minister urged employers and human resource practitioners to give young job seekers opportunities beyond conventional qualifications, including through interviews, mentoring and professional engagement.
He also encouraged bootcamp participants to turn their ideas into practical solutions and build their innovations in Penang. — Bernama

Title: Najib’s lawyers seek immediate transfer home, say King’s decree must be executed today
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — Lawyers for Datuk Seri Najib Razak are contesting the Attorney General’s Chambers’ (AGC) decision to temporarily suspend his house arrest, demanding the former prime minister be transferred to his home immediately.
In a media statement today, the legal firm Messrs Shafee & Co. argued that the AGC’s “temporary suspension” of the house arrest order contradicts the King’s explicit decree issued this morning.
“His Majesty has now spoken. The AGC can honour that commitment in only one way: by allowing the
Titah
(decree) to be carried out today,” the statement read.
The legal team argued that the High Court’s “Order of Discharge on Payment of Fine” issued on November 6 cannot be used to extend Najib’s imprisonment, citing the order’s own recital that the fine has been paid.
“In law, payment of a fine discharges the liability to pay that fine. It cannot, by itself, bring a sentence of imprisonment to an end,” the statement said.
They further asserted that the Pardon is an exercise of the King’s prerogative under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution and is not subject to review by any court or the Attorney General.
The statement noted that the AGC issued a subsequent media statement 57 minutes after the King’s decree, which did not reference the royal order.
According to the legal team, Najib remains in Kajang Prison as of the statement’s issuance, with no effect yet given to the King’s decree.
They have requested the Commissioner General of Prisons to transfer Najib to his residence at No. 11, Jalan Langgak Duta, Taman Duta, Kuala Lumpur.
“His Majesty’s order must be carried out today,” the statement read.

Title: Nancy wants 42,000 men to seek health support and join family decisions
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 7 — The Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development (KPWKM) is targeting 42,000 men to benefit from government-provided well-being services for men, as part of efforts to raise awareness of the importance of healthcare among them.
Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the initiative also encouraged men to seek relevant health information and services with their partners, particularly when making decisions about family health.
“I urge men to seek relevant information and services together with their partners when making decisions about family health,” she said at the Selangor International Trade Centre (SITC) here today.
She was speaking at the November National Family Month 2026 celebration, which was launched by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and attended by his wife, Bandar Tun Razak MP Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, Deputy Women, Family and Community Development Minister Lim Hui Ying, and Selangor State Executive Councillor for Women and Community Welfare Anfaal Saari.
Nancy said the government had allocated RM4.355 billion to KPWKM under Budget 2027, an increase of RM168 million from the previous year.
Of this amount, almost RM3.3 billion was allocated for welfare assistance to strengthen the social safety net and the well-being of those in need.
She said couples facing fertility challenges could also benefit from the Fertility Treatment Assistance and Infertility Advocacy Programme (BuAI), run by the National Population and Family Development Board (LPPKN), which aims to help 2,000 eligible couples receive treatment assistance.
In 2025, a total of 82,679 individuals benefited from the programme, while 1,658 Intrauterine Insemination (IUI) treatment cycles were carried out, resulting in 184 recorded pregnancies.
She said the achievement demonstrated the importance of early detection of fertility problems and access to treatment by qualified specialists. — Bernama

Title: All eyes on Nov 14 as police strengthen readiness for Melaka vote
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 7 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) is strengthening its level of preparedness to ensure public safety and order are maintained throughout the 16th Melaka State Election, which will be held on Nov 14.
According to a post on the Melaka Police Facebook page, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail, in his address during a working visit to the Melaka Contingent Police Headquarters (IPK) yesterday, touched on several matters, including duty assignment, security management and the responsibilities of every personnel in ensuring the smooth conduct of the election process.
“He emphasised that all members of the force must always maintain professionalism, integrity and discipline while carrying out their duties, and ensure that all actions are guided by the law and established standard operating procedures (SOPs),” it added.
According to the post, Mohd Khalid also reminded PDRM personnel to safeguard the confidentiality of official information, strengthen esprit de corps and ensure compliance with the chain of command and control to guarantee the effectiveness of every assignment.
In the same address, he also emphasised the importance of the welfare, safety and physical and mental health of all personnel.
“Supervising officers are also reminded to always pay attention to the needs and welfare of personnel under their supervision, ensuring that their motivation and commitment to carrying out their duties remain at the highest level,” it added.
During the visit, Mohd Khalid also inspected the Melaka State Election Operations Room to gain an overview of operational preparations and the mechanisms for coordinating personnel deployment, and was briefed on the current security situation, local issues, and the contingent’s strategic planning.
“He (Mohd Khalid) also emphasised that the success of the assignments for the 16th Melaka State Election depends on the unity, discipline and preparedness of all PDRM personnel in ensuring that the election is conducted in a peaceful and controlled environment,” it added.
Mohd Khalid subsequently continued his visit to the Melaka Tengah District Police Headquarters (IPD), where he addressed the personnel, urging them to remain prepared, strengthen cooperation and give their full commitment in carrying out their entrusted responsibilities.
Polling is on Nov 14, with early voting set for Nov 10.
For updates on the state election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. — Bernama

Title: Saifuddin Nasution wants schools, police and health authorities to share data on at-risk students
Article:
KULIM, Nov 7 — The Ministry of Home Affairs (KDN), the Ministry of Education (MOE), and the Ministry of Health (MOH) must strengthen their cooperation and information-sharing to address various security issues and create a safe school ecosystem.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said these three ministries cannot work in isolation when dealing with the various issues that arise within schools.
He noted that this necessity was among the matters discussed during a meeting of the Police-Ministry of Education Consultative Committee, held last week at the Police Training Centre (Pulapol).
“One of the points I raised concerns student profiling. For instance, there are students who require treatment and consultation with a psychiatrist, yet the school authorities lack access to such information, which is held by the Ministry of Health,” he said.
He made these remarks to reporters after attending the ‘Semarak Kebudayaan Masyarakat Kedah Bersama PDRM 2026’ programme here today.
He was asked to comment on media reports regarding the police’s arrest of two teenagers believed to be suppliers in a case involving a school student in Negeri Sembilan who vaped using an electronic cigarette containing drugs.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan was reported as saying that the arrested suspects include a 17-year-old student (a schoolmate of the victim) and an 18-year-old male who is no longer in school.
Saifuddin Nasution emphasised that collaboration among the three ministries is crucial, given that the school security ecosystem encompasses approximately 5.2 million students across 12,000 schools nationwide, a situation that necessitates information-sharing and integrated action among the relevant agencies.
Meanwhile, he noted that the use of vapes among students has also become a point of concern, as the contents of vape liquids — which may include a variety of substances — can complicate police investigations.
He explained that some substances may contain toxic components that have not yet been officially classified as poisons; this creates challenges for the police in completing investigations and bringing cases to the prosecution stage.
He said existing collaboration between the police and schools which includes the deployment of police liaison officers and the involvement of the National Anti-Drug Agency (AADK) needs to be expanded to also include the Ministry of Health (MOH).
“The issue is not limited to vape use among students; it also encompasses various other activities, such as bullying and accidents occurring within school premises,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Two step-sisters killed after car skids and crashes on PLUS highway near Tanjong Malim
Article:
IPOH, Nov 7 — Two step-siblings died when the vehicle they were in skidded in an accident at Kilometre 388 of the North-South Expressway (Plus) southbound, near Tanjong Malim today.
Muallim district police chief Supt Khalid Mohamad said an 18-year-old girl was pronounced dead at the scene, while a six-year-old girl who suffered severe injuries died while receiving treatment at the Slim River Hospital.
He said the driver, a 27-year-old man, and another female passenger, aged 20, sustained injuries and were taken to the same hospital for further treatment.
“In the incident at about 8.30am, a vehicle travelling from Perlis towards Kuala Lumpur is believed to have lost control before veering off to the left shoulder of the road and crashing into the road barrier,” he said in a statement today.
Khalid said the case was classified under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 and further investigations are being conducted to identify the actual cause of the accident.
He urged witnesses to the accident to contact the investigating officer, Inspector Muhammad Taufiq Abd Aziz, at 016-4184507 to assist with the investigation.
Earlier, Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant director (Operations) Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said a team from the Tanjong Malim Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to the scene after receiving a call regarding the accident at 8.35am. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi says online banking remains safe despite cyberattacks and Bank Rakyat hack
Article:
DOHA, Nov 7 — The country’s online banking system and financial transactions remain secure despite attempted cyberattacks by non-state actors, including a recent hacking incident involving Bank Rakyat’s website, Communications Minister and Madani government spokesperson Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said.
He said the hacking attempts detected so far had not resulted in data theft or affected the country’s online banking operations.
“We have identified attempts by non-state actors to launch cyberattacks, including hacking, but so far there has been no data theft or disruption to online banking systems.
“So, our banking and financial sectors remain secure, and online transactions are safe,” he said when asked by a Malaysian about the latest cyberattacks targeting the country, particularly the hacking of Bank Rakyat’s website, after attending the bowling event at the 2026 Malaysian Games in Qatar (Suqma 2026) here today.
Malaysia’s Ambassador to Qatar Faizal Razali and Malaysian Association of Qatar (MAQ) president Dr Mohd Faris Khamidi were also present.
On the hacking incident involving Bank Rakyat’s website, Fahmi said it was confined to changes to the website’s appearance and involved a third-party-managed site.
“In the latest development, Bank Rakyat reported that its third-party-managed website had been hacked, but the incident was limited to web defacement and the website had been taken over,” he said.
He said Bank Rakyat had blocked access to the affected server and redirected users to the i-Rakyat website, which the bank fully owns.
Meanwhile, Fahmi said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had ordered the National Security Council (MKN) to review potential security threats to various national infrastructure facilities, particularly hybrid threats, as early as the beginning of last week.
He said the exercise involved examining internet infrastructure, websites and databases to ensure continued protection of the country’s digital assets.
“At yesterday’s Cabinet meeting, the Prime Minister called for a more thorough review of cybersecurity across all government assets, banking institutions and government-linked companies, including by the National Cyber Security Agency and the MKN,” he said.
Fahmi is leading the Malaysian delegation to the 2026 International Telecommunication Union Plenipotentiary Conference (ITU PP-26), from Nov 6 to 11, an important platform for the country’s participation in international discussions and cooperation on telecommunications and digital technology.
His working visit to Doha also includes efforts to retain Malaysia’s seat on the ITU Council for the 2027-2030 term. — Bernama

Title: Flood evacuees in Selangor, Perak nearly triple to over 4,000 in hours
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — The flood situation in Selangor and Perak continued to worsen, with the number of evacuees at temporary relief centres (PPS) rising to 4,068 this afternoon from 1,404 this morning.
In
SELANGOR
, the number of flood evacuees still sheltering at PPS this afternoon rose to 3,798 from 128 families at two centres, compared with 1,206 from 316 families at nine centres this morning.
According to the Social Welfare Department’s (JKM) InfoBencana portal, PPS Sekolah Agama Batu Lapan Ijok is sheltering 2,999 evacuees from 67 families, while 799 evacuees from 61 families are at Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Parit Mahang.
Meanwhile, in
PERAK
, the number of flood and storm evacuees rose to 270 from 79 families this afternoon, compared with 198 from 58 families this morning, across the Hilir Perak and Manjung districts.
The State Disaster Management Committee Secretariat (JBPN) said in a statement that the number of evacuees at PPS Dewan Majlis Perbandaran Teluk Intan (MPTI) Langkap remained at 137 from 40 victims, while the number at PPS Dewan Rumah Rehat MPTI rose to 107 from 32 families.
Meanwhile, 26 people from seven families affected by the storm are still sheltering at PPS Dewan Komuniti Manjung.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department has forecast rain in all districts tonight. — Bernama

Title: AG seeks audience with King to clarify Najib’s house arrest issue, says Anwar
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 7 — Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar has requested an audience with His Majesty, Sultan Ibrahim, to discuss former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest in his SRC International case, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today.
Anwar stressed that the Agong’s power to grant pardons was not being disputed, but said there was a legal issue involving Najib’s 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) case that required clarification by the courts.
“I have asked for the Attorney General to immediately meet the Agong to ‘
mohon ampun
’ (apologise) and explain why that decision was accepted for the SRC case, but there is a problem as it involves the second case, which is the 1MDB case.
“So to explain and maybe we need a few days to decide after referring to the judiciary. I also only leave it to the Attorney General to elaborate on this case, because this is not the prime minister’s jurisdiction,” he told reporters after launching the National Family Month celebrations at the Selangor International Trade Centre (SITC) here.
Anwar later added that the AG had already requested an audience with the King to explain the house arrest issue.
Earlier, Anwar said he wanted to avoid this house arrest matter from becoming politicised.
“But I want to explain that the Yang di-Pertuan Agong’s powers is not disputed, that’s the first, that’s in the SRC case as stated by the Pardons Board.
“The case that arises in the second case, whether it can be carried out or not, that is a decision that will be finalised by the Attorney General and the judiciary, that’s all,” he said, adding that the dissatisfaction by some on the house arrest issue is beyond his jurisdiction.
Anwar had also said preparations had been made to carry out the house arrest in the SRC International case in line with the Agong’s pardon, but said the Attorney General faced constraints as the matter was related to the 1MDB case, and that was why a few days are needed to finalise it.
Separately, the Prime Minister’s Office this evening issued a statement to confirm that the Attorney General had today requested for an audience with His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim to apologise and to express his stand in complying with the King’s decree on the conditional pardon in Najib’s SRC International case.
“The Attorney General will also explain the legal matter that arose from the High Court’s Order of Discharge following the payment of the RM50 million fine, and that has to be decided by the courts as it gives an impact on the date when the jail sentence in the 1MDB case will start,” the brief statement said.
In 2024, a royal pardon over Najib’s SRC International case resulted in the reduction of his 12-year jail term to six years, and his RM210 million fine to RM50 million.
On September 18, Najib was given a conditional pardon in his SRC International case, which allowed him to serve the rest of his jail term under house arrest until August 23, 2028, if he pays the RM50 million fine.
Separately, Najib is facing a 15-year jail term in his 1MDB case, with the High Court in December 2025 ordering the imprisonment to be carried out immediately after the end of his SRC International jail term.
Najib is currently appealing his 1MDB conviction and sentence, and the High Court had on October 14 rejected his bid to stay or to pause the carrying out of the 1MDB sentence.
Umno yesterday paid the RM50 million fine on Najib’s behalf, but he is currently still at Kajang Prison as the Attorney General yesterday highlighted the need to clarify legal matters linked to the house arrest.
Earlier today, Istana Negara issued a statement saying that His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim’s conditional pardon order was clear and unambiguous and unrelated to any other cases against Najib, and said there should not be any confusion over its interpretation or prolonged uncertainty over its implementation.
Istana Negara also said that any dispute of the conditional pardon order would amount to disobeying the King’s order.
Prior to Anwar’s remarks this afternoon, the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) today issued a lengthy statement that explained it was not disputing or setting aside or intended to suspend the Agong’s conditional pardon order for Najib’s house arrest.
The AGC said it was necessary for the court to decide on uncertainties regarding whether the RM50 million fine payment meant the SRC International sentence had been fully resolved or if Najib still had to serve the remaining term on house arrest.
