Title: Bukit Aman suspects cocaine-in-shoes arrest at Hong Kong airport linked to Malaysia drug bust
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — The arrest of a Hong Kong man with about one kilogramme of cocaine concealed in his shoes at Hong Kong International Airport after arriving from Kuala Lumpur last Wednesday is believed to be linked to an international drug trafficking syndicate recently crippled by the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM).
Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the suspected link was based on similarities in the modus operandi, type of drugs and trafficking destinations, namely Hong Kong, Japan and Indonesia.
“We believe the syndicate has been crippled following the arrest of a Hong Kong national believed to be the syndicate leader and a local recruiter, as announced at yesterday’s press conference,” he said when contacted today.
Media reports today said a 36-year-old Hong Kong man was arrested last Wednesday after customs officers found cocaine estimated to be worth HK$600,000 (RM311,000) during an inspection at Hong Kong International Airport following his arrival from Malaysia.
Hussein said PDRM had been informed by Hong Kong authorities of the arrest and drug seizure, adding that both sides had exchanged relevant information.
He said the cocaine did not originate from Malaysia, but the country was believed to have been used as a transit hub before the drugs were smuggled to their intended destinations through Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) or Penang International Airport.
Yesterday, media reports said PDRM had arrested four individuals, including a Hong Kong national believed to be the mastermind of the syndicate, during an operation at a homestay in Brickfields here on Nov 5.
During the operation, police also seized 450 grammes of cocaine and two pairs of shoes believed to have been intended for two individuals recruited as drug mules.
The syndicate, believed to have been active since September, was found to have recruited Malaysians to smuggle drugs overseas.
Those recruited included five individuals arrested by authorities at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport in Jakarta and another five at Haneda International Airport in Tokyo in September and October. — Bernama

Title: Tourism Ministry open to helping international event organisers facing funding challenges, says Tiong
Article:
SIBU, Nov 7 — The Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture (Motac) is prepared to consider collaborating with and providing assistance to organisers of international events in Malaysia, particularly those facing financial constraints.
Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing said the move was aimed at encouraging more international events to be held in the country while attracting greater participation from overseas.
“This is in line with the ministry’s aim to strengthen Malaysia’s presence on the international stage by hosting events that attract participants from various countries,” he told reporters at the International Archery Coaching and Wellness Forum and Workshop 2026 here today.
He said such events could also attract more visitors and serve as a platform for local and international participants to share knowledge, experiences and skills.
“We hope next year’s forum and coaching workshop can be expanded to involve more participating countries,” he said.
Tiong said the ministry would also explore possible forms of collaboration and assistance to help organisers address their financial challenges. — Bernama

Title: DAP yet to discuss replacing Anthony Loke as transport minister, says party vice-chairman
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — DAP has yet to discuss a replacement for Transport Minister Anthony Loke, whose resignation remains conditional on former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak returning home to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.
DAP vice-chairman Syahredzan Johan said discussions about a potential successor would be premature because Loke’s resignation had not taken effect, the
New Straits Times
reported.
“For now, his resignation has not taken effect until Datuk Seri Najib sets foot in his house, so it is inappropriate to discuss who the replacement will be,” he said when contacted.
Syahredzan also stressed that Cabinet appointments remained the prerogative of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who would consult DAP’s leadership before making any decision.
“Cabinet appointments are the prerogative of the prime minister. Of course, the prime minister will make a decision after discussions with the DAP secretary-general himself,” he said.
Loke, who is also DAP secretary-general, reaffirmed yesterday that his resignation would take effect only when Najib physically returned home to begin serving his sentence under house arrest.
He had submitted his resignation letter to Anwar on September 28 in protest against the conditional royal pardon granted to Najib, reflecting DAP’s opposition to the house arrest arrangement.
The uncertainty over Loke’s departure follows the payment of Najib’s RM50 million fine yesterday, fulfilling a key condition of the royal pardon.
The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) subsequently sought a temporary deferment of Najib’s transfer to house arrest, citing unresolved legal questions over the effect of the conditional pardon and a court discharge order.
The AGC said clarification was needed on the implications for Najib’s separate 15-year prison sentence in the 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) case, which is under appeal.
Istana Negara, however, maintained today that the conditional pardon granted by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim was clear and unambiguous, and that all its conditions had been fulfilled.
The AGC has said it is not challenging the King’s constitutional power to grant pardons but is seeking judicial clarification to ensure that the relevant orders are implemented lawfully.
Najib, 73, has been imprisoned since August 2022 following his conviction over the misappropriation of RM42 million belonging to SRC International, a former subsidiary of 1MDB.
On September 18, Sultan Ibrahim granted Najib a conditional royal pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine and other stipulated conditions.

Title: Teenager, 19, dies after being stabbed during alleged argument at Sibu park
Article:
SIBU, Nov 7 — A 19-year-old youth died after being stabbed in the chest during an incident at a public park along Jalan Gambir here around midnight last night.
The victim was reportedly at the park with a group of young men and women when an argument broke out, allegedly leading to the stabbing.
He sustained a stab wound to the chest and was rushed to hospital for emergency treatment but later succumbed to his injuries.
It is understood that nearby residents heard a woman screaming from the direction of the park, prompting them to alert the police.
Police are believed to have arrested two men in their 20s to assist in investigations.
When contacted today, Sibu District Police Chief ACP Abang Zainal Abidin Abang Ahmad confirmed that the case was still under investigation.
“The case is still under further investigation,” he said. — The Borneo Post

Title: Security presence disappears from Najib’s Taman Duta residence as house arrest remains on hold
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — The security presence outside former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s residence was nowhere to be seen today, a day after the Taman Duta property was placed under tight security ahead of his anticipated return under house arrest.
According to
Astro Awani
, no police officers or Prisons Department vehicles were visible outside the Jalan Langgak Duta residence, while yellow security tape restricting access to the property had also been removed.
The scene contrasted sharply with Friday, when security personnel controlled access to the residence, allowing only authorised individuals and vehicles to enter or leave.
The heightened security came as preparations were made for Najib’s expected return after he paid a RM50 million fine in the SRC International corruption case, fulfilling a key condition of a royal pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028.
However, the move was put on hold after the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) called for further legal clarification on the implementation of the conditional pardon.
Despite the absence of security personnel today, local and international journalists remained stationed near the residence, awaiting further developments.
Najib’s residence was officially gazetted as a prison on Friday under Section 3 of the Prisons Act 1995, following a declaration by Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
The designation covers the property and its surrounding land, allowing it to be used for the detention of individuals in lawful custody.
In a statement today, the AGC called for an urgent court determination on whether Najib’s SRC International prison sentence remains in force or has legally ended following the payment of the fine.
It said the distinction was crucial because Najib’s separate 15-year prison sentence in the 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) corruption case was ordered to begin after the completion of his SRC International sentence.
The AGC also rejected allegations that it was challenging the authority of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, maintaining that its request for judicial clarification was intended to ensure the royal decree and existing court orders were implemented lawfully.
The clarification came after Istana Negara said the conditional pardon granted to Najib was clear and unambiguous, warning that any attempt to dispute the decree could amount to defying the King’s order.
Najib, 73, has been serving a prison sentence since August 2022 following his conviction for offences involving RM42 million in SRC International funds.
His original 12-year sentence was reduced to six years under a partial royal pardon in 2024, while his RM210 million fine was cut to RM50 million.
A subsequent conditional pardon granted on September 18 this year allowed him to serve the remaining term under house arrest, subject to payment of the fine and compliance with stipulated conditions.

Title: Integrity must go hand in hand with academic success, Perlis Raja Muda tells UniSIRAJ graduates
Article:
KANGAR, Nov 7 — Universiti Islam Antarabangsa Tuanku Syed Sirajuddin (UniSIRAJ) graduates must be trustworthy and uphold integrity, respect differences and stand by the truth - qualities that should guide them as they embark on their careers and future lives.
Raja Muda of Perlis Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra Jamalullail, who is also UniSIRAJ Chancellor, said knowledge developed one’s ability to think and solve problems, while good manners reflected one’s values.
“Ensure that academic excellence and expertise are always accompanied by strong moral values and principles,” he said at the 9th UniSIRAJ Convocation Ceremony at Dewan 2020 here today.
Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra said that in an era of artificial intelligence (AI) and digital advancement, the pursuit of knowledge must always go hand in hand with noble values and strong principles.
He also said graduates should build their careers diligently, discharge their responsibilities well and leverage their expertise to generate ideas and solutions that would add value to organisations and society.
“Success is not merely about positions, income or personal achievements, but also about the benefits one brings to others. The journey after convocation will not necessarily be easy.
“Failures, competition and changes will test one’s abilities. Turn every challenge into an opportunity to learn, address weaknesses and improve one’s capabilities. Face them with patience, perseverance and faith in Allah, without compromising one’s principles or self-respect,” he said.
Meanwhile, he said knowledge and expertise must translate into actions that bring benefits to others. Those who become leaders should lead with integrity, educators should teach with a strong sense of responsibility, while professionals should carry out their duties conscientiously and prioritise the interests of humanity.
Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra said every position and opportunity should be regarded as a platform to serve others.
At the convocation ceremony, the Raja Muda of Perlis also presented the Chancellor’s Award (Martabat Al-Syaraf Al-Ula) to Maryam Al Adzra Mohd Zawawi, a Bachelor of Hadith graduate from the Faculty of Al-Quran and Sunnah, who achieved a cumulative grade point average (CGPA) of 3.95.
A total of 277 UniSIRAJ graduates received their respective Doctor of Philosophy (PhD), Master’s, Bachelor’s and Diploma scrolls at the ceremony. — Bernama

Title: The journey home begins: Deepavali rush brings slow traffic to major highways across Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — Traffic on several major highways across the country began to slow down this afternoon as vehicle numbers increased, with members of the public starting their journeys ahead of Deepavali tomorrow.
A Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) spokesperson said the affected routes included the northbound stretch of the North-South Expressway (PLUS) E1 from Trolak to Bidor, Gopeng to Simpang Pulai, Alor Pongsu to Jawi, and Perai to Bertam, along with the southbound stretch from Perai to Juru.

“Traffic was also slow at the Johor Causeway, from Woodlands Checkpoint (CIQ) in Singapore to Sultan Iskandar CIQ in Johor in the northbound direction, while congestion was reported on the Second Link Expressway, from the Second Link Bridge to Sultan Abu Bakar CIQ in Johor, also northbound,” they said when contacted today.

Meanwhile, on the Sungai Besi Expressway (BESRAYA), traffic was slow on the northbound stretches from Bandar Tasik Selatan to Kuchai and Serdang to Pekan Sungai Besi.
On the Damansara-Puchong Expressway (LDP), the affected stretches were Kelana Jaya to Damansara Utama and Bandar Bukit Puchong to Jalan Majlis in the northbound direction, while traffic was slow from Penchala to Damansara Utama and Sunway to Bandar Bukit Puchong in the southbound direction.
On the Kajang Dispersal Link Expressway (SILK), traffic was slow from Country Heights to Putrajaya via the South Klang Valley Expressway (SKVE) in the westbound direction, as well as from Kajang Prima to Kajang Perdana in the eastbound direction.
Also affected was the Kajang-Seremban Expressway (LEKAS), with slow traffic from Kajang Selatan to Semenyih in the southbound direction, while on the South Klang Valley Expressway (SKVE), traffic was slow from MAEPS Serdang to Sultan Idris Shah Hospital in Serdang in the eastbound direction.
The public can obtain the latest traffic updates via the 24-hour hotline at 1800-88-7752 and through the X platforms @plustrafik and @llmtrafik. — Bernama

Title: Umno leaders lodge police reports, Dr Akmal demands action on Najib’s house arrest delay
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — Several Umno leaders in Johor have lodged a police report over the delay in implementing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest, as Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhammad Akmal Saleh called for similar reports to be filed nationwide.
Pontian Umno chief Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan, who is also a party supreme council member, lodged the report at the Benut police station at 12.30pm today, accompanied by his deputy Mohd Sumali Reduan, division vice-chief Jamaludin Abd Majid and several grassroots leaders.
“A police report was lodged over the delay in implementing the house arrest order for Najib, which should have been carried out,” Ahmad said in a Facebook post.
Meanwhile, Dr Akmal said Umno Youth branches at state and division levels would lodge police reports to seek an investigation into whether any laws had been breached in delaying the implementation of the royal pardon and related court order.
In a statement today, he urged the government to immediately implement the conditional pardon granted by His Majesty, Sultan Ibrahim, maintaining that all stipulated conditions had been fulfilled.
“On November 6, all conditions were met. The RM50 million fine was paid at the Kuala Lumpur High Court, which then issued a sealed order allowing Datuk Seri Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest. The Home Ministry also gazetted his residence as a prison under Section 3 of the Prisons Act 1995,” Akmal said.
He argued that further legal proceedings should not delay the implementation of the order.
“Umno Youth demands that His Majesty’s decree be implemented immediately. Any further court reference should not be used as grounds to stall a decree that His Majesty has confirmed to be clear and unambiguous,” he said.
Pasir Gudang Umno Youth was also expected to lodge a similar police report against the Attorney General at the Seri Alam district police headquarters.
The moves follow the Attorney General’s Chambers’ (AGC) call yesterday for Najib’s house arrest to be temporarily deferred pending clarification of legal questions surrounding his conditional pardon.
The AGC said the questions centred on whether payment of the RM50 million fine meant Najib’s remaining prison sentence in the SRC International case continued under house arrest or was deemed completed.
It said the interpretation could affect when Najib’s separate prison sentence in the 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) case should begin.
In a further statement today, the AGC denied attempting to override the King’s authority, maintaining that judicial clarification was necessary to prevent conflicting interpretations of the court orders and ensure their lawful implementation.
Istana Negara, meanwhile, reaffirmed today that the conditional pardon granted on September 18 was clear and unambiguous, and that all stipulated conditions had been fulfilled.
The pardon allows Najib to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine and compliance with other conditions.
Najib has been imprisoned since August 2022 following his conviction over the misappropriation of RM42 million in SRC International funds.

Title: GrabCar’s auto-accept booking system breaches gig workers’ rights, tribunal rules
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 7 — The Gig Workers Tribunal (TPG) has ruled on three disputes involving e-hailing drivers and GrabCar Sdn Bhd, including awarding RM2,000 in compensation to one driver while upholding the deactivation of another driver’s account over misconduct involving passengers.
The Human Resources Ministry (Kesuma) said in a statement today that the three cases involved financial claims, the handling of digital platform systems and the deactivation of a driver’s account, which TPG deputy president Suzarika Sahak heard.
According to Kesuma, the tribunal partially upheld an e-hailing driver’s financial claim against GrabCar in the first case, involving earnings from Saver bookings and the ‘Cashback and Advance Booking’ incentive.
“The tribunal also awarded RM2,000 in compensation, together with interest at eight per cent per annum until full settlement.
“The tribunal also found that GrabCar’s use of the ‘Auto Accept’ and ‘Fast Cancel’ mechanisms on its digital platform violated Section 8(1)(b) and (c) of the Gig Workers Act 2025 (Act 872),” the ministry said, noting that the provisions safeguard gig workers’ right to know the type of service and the agreed payment before accepting a job.
In the second case, another e-hailing driver brought seven non-financial claims against GrabCar over how it handled and operated its digital platform.
“The tribunal found three breaches of Act 872, relating to temporary booking pauses, booking cancellation quotas and the ‘Auto Accept’ system,” it said, adding that the temporary suspension of bookings and the platform’s failure to explain the terms and duration of the measure were found to contravene Section 8(1)(a) and Section 8(2)(a) and (b) of the Act.
“The tribunal also found that the failure to clearly explain how cancellation quotas are set, what happens when the quota is reached and the options for cancelling bookings for reasonable reasons violated Section 8(2)(a) and (b) of the Act,” it said.
The statement also said that the operation of the ‘Auto Accept’ system, which resulted in bookings being accepted before drivers were informed of the type of service and the earnings offered, was also found to breach Section 8(1)(b) and (c) of Act 872.
In both cases, the tribunal recommended improvements under Subsection 42(3) of Act 872, including ensuring drivers are informed of the type of service and earnings before accepting a booking and given a reasonable and safe window to cancel, Kesuma said.
“The tribunal further recommended clearer terms governing temporary booking pauses, cancellation quotas, incentive programmes and booking restrictions, as well as better access to platform support personnel and a human review process for decisions made by automated systems,” it said.
In the third case, the tribunal upheld GrabCar’s decision to permanently deactivate a driver’s account after finding evidence of three incidents of misconduct towards passengers, involving inappropriate conversations, intimidating or threatening behaviour, and unwarranted personal questions.
“Although the deactivation of an account may affect a driver’s livelihood, the tribunal held that passenger safety and well-being must not be compromised. The driver’s claim was therefore dismissed,” Kesuma said.
The ministry emphasised that the three decisions reflected the tribunal’s balanced approach to upholding gig workers’ rights, ensuring passenger safety and protecting the interests of e-hailing platform operators.
The ministry also pledged to strengthen enforcement of Act 872 through the TPG, an independent, fair and effective mechanism for resolving disputes, to support a more transparent, sustainable and accountable gig economy. — Bernama

Title: Bank Rakyat blames third-party glitch for website outage, says customer funds and data safe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — Bank Rakyat said today that a disruption to its corporate website was caused by a technical problem involving a third-party service provider, assuring customers that their deposits, personal information and banking services remained unaffected.
In a statement posted on Facebook, the bank said the disruption was confined to its corporate website, while its banking systems and operations continued to function normally.
It said efforts were under way to restore access, with customers able to continue conducting transactions through alternative digital channels.
“Customers can continue to carry out their banking transactions as usual through alternative channels, including the iRakyat website, iRakyat mobile application, BRICK, QR2E and i-bizRAKYAT,” the bank said.
“We apologise for the inconvenience caused and appreciate our customers’ patience. Further updates on the matter will be provided from time to time.
“The security and interests of our customers remain Bank Rakyat’s top priority.”
Separately, technology news portal Lowyat.NET reported that several Bank Rakyat banking webpages, including its iRakyat online banking login page, had been defaced in a suspected cyberattack late yesterday.
The bank has not confirmed a cyberattack, attributing the disruption instead to a technical issue involving a third-party service provider.
The clarification follows an earlier advisory issued at about 11.30pm yesterday, when Bank Rakyat informed customers that its corporate website was temporarily inaccessible, according to Bernama.
The bank advised customers to use alternative digital banking platforms but did not specify the cause of the disruption or indicate when access would be restored.

Title: Penang pledges land titles for all 28 Tamil schools, with five secured so far
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 7 — The Penang State Government is committed to ensuring that all 28 Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan Tamil (SJKT) in the state secure their respective land titles, as part of efforts to strengthen educational facilities.
Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said as of June, land titles had been successfully secured for five schools, with plans to secure titles for another five within the next two to three years.
“In its efforts to strengthen educational facilities, the state government is also committed to ensuring that all 28 SJKT in Penang secure their respective land titles.
“One of the commitments fulfilled by the state government is the provision of a 2.368-acre site for the relocation project of SJKT Rajaji in Air Itam,” he said in a message delivered in conjunction with the Deepavali 2026 celebrations today.
Chow noted that the state government is also focusing on the development of Tamil-medium education, including initiatives to enhance digital skills and broaden students’ exposure to the fields of Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM).
Chow mentioned that in April, a total of RM2.42 million was allocated for the development of Tamil-medium schools in Penang. Of this amount, RM1.34 million was channelled through the Penang Education Council (PEC) to strengthen digital infrastructure and STEM competencies.
He added that RM768,901 was distributed to the 28 SJKTs via their respective Parent-Teacher Associations (PIBG) for the maintenance and improvement of learning facilities while RM194,400 was allocated to 11 kindergartens located within SJKT premises to support early childhood education.
Furthermore, Chow emphasised that educational progress must go hand in hand with efforts to preserve language and culture citing, for instance, the ‘Free Tamil Language Class’ initiative organised by the Village Community Management Council (MPKK) of Lebuh Pasar.
He expressed hope that more such initiatives would be implemented to ensure that linguistic and cultural heritage continues to be preserved among the younger generation.
Meanwhile, Chow said the state government will continue to collaborate with the federal government, educational institutions, civil society organisations, and the private sector to expand opportunities for inclusive development through the Madani Budget. 2027.
He said these efforts include support through the National Entrepreneur Group Economic Fund (Tekun Nasional), Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia (AIM), and the Malaysian Indian Community Transformation Unit (Mitra), specifically aimed at empowering small-scale entrepreneurs and youths of Indian descent.
“Indeed, meaningful development is one which creates opportunities, enhances well-being, and ensures that every community can enjoy the benefits of the state’s progress,” he said.
He also expressed hope that this year’s Deepavali celebration would foster a spirit of goodwill and strengthen societal unity for the sake of a better future for Penang.
He added that the diversity of races, religions, languages, and cultures in Penang serves as a strength that unites the community in building a shared future. — Bernama

Title: Jalaluddin denies plot to oust Negeri Sembilan MB, says no-confidence vote never discussed
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 7 — Negeri Sembilan Umno chief Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias has denied plotting to oust Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim, dismissing speculation that a vote of no confidence was being planned amid uncertainty over the state’s political leadership.
Jalaluddin said no such move had been discussed at a meeting of the state Umno leadership today, insisting that claims of rival factions within the party were unfounded.
According to
Utusan Malaysia
, Jalaluddin was speaking after a Negeri Sembilan Umno liaison committee meeting at Wisma Umno in Seremban today.
“Have you heard me say I want to bring down the menteri besar? No. I made that clear at the meeting earlier.
“Even this morning, there were still claims that we would decide on a vote of no confidence against the menteri besar today, when there is no such thing. Please stop,” he said, according to the Malay-language daily.
His remarks came after Ismail declined to comment on speculation that Jalaluddin, the Pertang assemblyman and Jelebu MP, could replace him as menteri besar.
“As of today, I am still the menteri besar,” Ismail told reporters yesterday, offering no further comment on the claims surrounding his position.
Speculation about a possible leadership challenge surfaced last month when FMT reported, citing an unnamed source, that Negeri Sembilan Umno was considering a no-confidence motion against Ismail.
Jalaluddin denied the claim, while Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said he would prevent any such move.
The latest speculation comes just three months after Ismail was sworn in on August 2, following a state election in which Barisan Nasional (BN) won 18 seats, Pakatan Harapan 11 and Perikatan Nasional (PN) seven.
Jalaluddin also rejected suggestions that separate camps had emerged within Negeri Sembilan Umno, including factions allegedly aligned with him and Ismail.
He said assemblymen should put aside perceptions of internal divisions and focus on their responsibilities to voters.
He urged state leaders to support one another rather than engage in disputes that could distract from the administration’s work.
Addressing questions about his audience with the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, Jalaluddin said the meeting had taken place at the ruler’s request.
He said he would comply whenever summoned by the ruler, both as a party leader and as a subject.
Jalaluddin expressed hope that the state’s political tensions could be resolved soon if all parties worked towards unity.

Title: Mardi to tighten safety procedures across Malaysia after worker dies from bee stings, says D-G
Article:
CHUKAI, Nov 7 — The Malaysian Agricultural Research and Development Institute (Mardi) will tighten its safety standard operating procedures (SOPs) and improve safety management for field staff following the death of one of its employees after being stung by bees at the Mardi Kemaman Station in Ayer Putih, near here, last month.
Mardi director-general Dr Sanimah Simoh said the measures would be implemented at all Mardi research stations nationwide to ensure that occupational safety and health remained a priority and to minimise the risk of accidents.
She said the matter had been discussed at the Mardi senior management meeting, with several follow-up measures planned to strengthen compliance with existing safety SOPs.
“Mardi management takes staff safety seriously, especially for those working in the field. We have discussed this matter at the meeting, and follow-up measures will be implemented to tighten the SOPs and ensure that all work instructions are complied with.
“Meetings on occupational safety and health will also be held regularly to ensure that safety aspects are continuously monitored and improvements can be made from time to time,” she said in a statement today.
Meanwhile, Sanimah said the Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH) was scheduled to conduct a comprehensive safety audit at the Mardi Kemaman farm in the near future.
She said she had also instructed the management of Terengganu Mardi to take precautionary measures to ensure that the area was ready before the audit was conducted.
“I urge all Mardi staff, particularly those carrying out field duties, to remain vigilant and always comply with the prescribed procedures and work instructions,” she said.
The media had previously reported that a Mardi employee died after being stung by bees while collecting honey at a farm at the Mardi Kemaman Station.
Kemaman police chief Supt Mohd Razi Rosli said the incident occurred on the morning of October 24, when the victim, Hafizul Mat Nor, 40, who worked as a general worker, was at the farm with a colleague. — Bernama

Title: ECRL Phase 1 completed, on track for Dec 12 launch
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — The East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) has reached a major milestone with the completion and handover of Phase 1 from Kota Bharu, Kelantan, to Gombak, Selangor, to the project owner, Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL).
MRL, in a statement today, said China Communications Construction (ECRL) Sdn Bhd (CCCECRL), the Engineering, Procurement, Construction and Commissioning (EPCC) contractor for the project, officially handed over the 523-kilometre (km) Kota Bharu-Gombak alignment today, marking that the railway system is fully ready for commercial operations, scheduled to commence on Dec 12.
It said the handover coincides with the commencement of the ECRL Trial Operations Programme today, which will run until Dec 2 as the final phase of preparations ahead of the launch of passenger services.
The programme, conducted by ECRL Operation Sdn Bhd (EOSB), a 50:50 joint venture between MRL and CCCECRL, will assess operational readiness, service efficiency, station management and passenger experience in a real operating environment.
MRL chief executive officer Datuk Seri Darwis Abdul Razak said each journey during the trial operations would provide an opportunity to assess passenger experience and operational arrangements to ensure the service was safe and reliable before opening to the public.
“We know many Malaysians are looking forward to experiencing ECRL. The value of the railway will be felt in everyday journeys, whether they are travelling home to see family, travelling for work or education, or making journeys between the East Coast and the Klang Valley,” he said in a statement.
According to the statement, the first trial journey departed from the Gombak Integrated Terminal station at 7 am today, and arrived at KotaSAS station in Kuantan, Pahang, at 8.28 am, completing the journey in 88 minutes with 170 passengers onboard and reaching speeds of up to 160 km per hour.
The train subsequently departed KotaSAS at 9.33 am, arriving at Kuala Terengganu station at 9.53 am before continuing its journey and reaching Kota Bharu station at 10.58 am.
It said, during the trial period, ECRL electric multiple unit (EMU) trains will operate according to the planned commercial passenger timetable, including the issuance of boarding passes and provision of cabin crew services, covering both express and transit services between Gombak and Kota Bharu in both directions.
Darwis said, backed by a modern and state-of-the-art railway system, ECRL’s commercial operations will serve as a catalyst for economic growth and sustainable development as well as enhance connectivity along its rail network.
“We anticipate the ECRL to spur investment opportunities, drive tourism growth, foster job creation, and develop new logistics hubs and industrial parks in the East Coast states,” he added.
The statement said the Phase 1 handover also encompasses a fully integrated railway network comprising 16 stations, including dedicated passenger stations and combined passenger and freight terminals, as well as 41 tunnels and 218 viaducts spanning 154 km.
Among the project’s major engineering achievements is the 16.39 km twin-bore Genting Tunnel, which holds two Malaysia Book of Records recognitions as the country’s Longest Railway Tunnel and Highest Overburden Railway Tunnel.
Meanwhile, CCCECRL managing director Deng Bo said the delivery of a fully operational railway system for ECRL Phase 1 represents a defining milestone for cross-peninsular connectivity.
“This is a fully integrated railway network where trains, stations, signalling, power supply and operational systems work seamlessly together. By handing over this entire rail ecosystem, we are providing Malaysia with a modern railway backbone that will transform regional travel and commerce.
“Our teams are now fully focused on supporting the final pre-operational preparations, ensuring the entire system meets the required standards for handover to MRL,” he said in a statement.
MRL said with the Phase 1 railway system successfully handed over, CCCECRL is now concentrating its resources on Phase 2, which extends the rail network from Gombak to its final maritime gateway at Port Klang in Selangor.
It said engineering and systems works for Phase 2 remain firmly on track, paving the way for full network integration of the entire 665 km network.
Upon completion, the ECRL will serve as a high-capacity land bridge connecting Kuantan Port and Port Klang, strengthening logistics connectivity and unlocking new economic opportunities across Peninsular Malaysia.
MRL said the ECRL fare structure, based on a dynamic pricing mechanism, was approved by the Cabinet last month, with Economy Class fares for the Gombak-Kota Bharu Transit service starting from RM125.
Further information on ticket sales and passenger services will be announced through ECRL’s official channels in mid-November. — Bernama

Title: Fomca’s 72-hour food stockpiling advice not a government directive, says Mat Sabu
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 7 — The government has not issued any directive for the public to stock up on food supplies for a 72-hour period as recommended by the Federation of Malaysian Consumer Associations (Fomca).
Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu advised consumers not to panic buy, but instead to continue shopping according to their daily needs as usual.
“We do acknowledge that we are concerned about the current situation, including cyber threats, but we have not yet reached the stage of issuing directives for the public to stockpile food supplies,” he said at a press conference after officiating the ‘
Himpunan Semarak Tani Jualan Agro Madani
’ in Bukit Katil here today.
Yesterday, Fomca advised consumers to stock up on food and basic necessities for a period of at least 72 hours, as a precautionary measure against potential supply disruptions due to global geopolitical uncertainties and natural disasters.
Commenting further, Mohamad assured that the national rice stock is currently sufficient for a period of six months and will continue to be increased.
“The supply of frozen fish is also guaranteed to be sufficient for the next eight months. So, there is no need for excessive purchases.
“Buying goods in excessive quantities will only create problems and make it difficult for other consumers to obtain supplies,” he said.
Mohamad said that the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security (KPKM) is also constantly assessing the current situation, including through collaboration with universities and researchers such as climate change experts.
As an initial preparatory step, he said the Malaysian Fisheries Development Authority (LKIM), along with private traders who have freezing facilities, have been asked to stock up especially on the people’s choice of fish in high demand in the market.
In another development, he said the government aims to implement 5,000 Agro Madani Sales programmes nationwide, compared to the 3,400 programmes that have been held so far.
Mohamad said this programme that allows consumers to buy goods at 10 to 30 per cent cheaper prices aims to ease the people’s cost of living burden, especially in rural and small town areas.
“We cannot hold programmes like these every day because local grocery stores also need to do business. So, we are holding it weekly to give people a chance to save money while also ensuring the sustainability of local traders,” he added.
Meanwhile, KPKM in a statement said that the Himpunan Semarak Tani @ Jualan Agro Madani (JAM) Mega Negeri Melaka 2026, which is taking place over three days from yesterday, aims to attract 20,000 visitors and benefit 30,000 households.
The ministry set the sales value at RM500,000, involving 109 sales and exhibition lots that brings together 83 entrepreneurs and exhibitors from departments and agencies.
Today’s programme also witnessed the handover of incentives amounting to RM437,450 to five entrepreneurs through the Agropreneur NextGen Start-Up Grant, the High Impact Product (HIP) Matching Grant, and the Market Development and Matching Incentive for Micro Products of the Agricultural-Based Industry (IAT) for Melaka State Entrepreneurs 2026.
“This initiative reflects KPKM’s commitment to empowering local agri-food entrepreneurs and supporting the development of high-impact products,” according to the statement.
KPKM announced that as of October 2026, the Melaka branch of the Federal Agricultural Marketing Authority (FAMA) has implemented 258 JAM programmes involving 3,300 entrepreneurs with a total sales value of RM5.87 million.
Overall, a total of 3,400 JAM programmes have been conducted nationwide from January to November 2026, with sales value exceeding RM80 million and savings for consumers amounting to RM26 million.
“This implementation also involves the participation of 55,000 entrepreneurs and the attendance of over 4.7 million visitors nationwide,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak polls: Fadillah dismisses candidacy speculation, says GPS machinery ready (VIDEO)
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 7 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Amar Fadillah Yusof has brushed off speculation that he may contest in the 13th Sarawak state election.
Asked by reporters whether there was any truth to speculation that he could be among the candidates in the upcoming polls, Fadillah said he was unaware of it.
“That is speculation, so there is no need to comment. I myself do not know,” he said.
Fadillah, who is also Petra Jaya MP and minister of energy transition and water transformation, was speaking to reporters after officiating the Royal Malaysia Police Sarawak Contingent futsal court at the Sarawak Contingent Police headquarters here on Saturday.
He was also asked about the key dates announced by the Election Commission (EC) for the state election.
Fadillah, who is Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB) senior vice president and Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) parliamentary chief whip, said PBB and GPS election machinery was already prepared, with preparations having been carried out since the previous state election.
“Actually, our work is carried out all the time. Since the last election, we have already started working. This is just the democratic process where we have to hold an election,” he said.
He said PBB’s election machinery was ready to assist all GPS component parties, with logistics and other arrangements already in place ahead of nomination day.
“All the groundwork has been arranged, including logistics and everything. We are ready and waiting for nomination day, after which the machinery will start going to the ground,” he said.
On the 14-day campaign period, the longest in Sarawak’s electoral history, Fadillah said GPS respected the EC’s decision and would prepare accordingly.
“That is the discretion or jurisdiction of the EC. As a party, we respect whatever decision is made.
“For us, we need to prepare ourselves. If it is 14 days, we prepare for 14 days. If it is 10 days, then we work for 10 days. That is the authority of the EC,” he said.
He said the election was ultimately about giving voters the opportunity to decide who would administer Sarawak for the next five years.
“The election is only for us to hand it back to the people to determine who will administer our state, particularly for the next five years,” he said. — The Borneo Post

Title: Kelantan tops list of 3,045 flood hotspots as ministry prepares for monsoon
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 7 — The Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (Petra) is enhancing its preparedness for the 2026/2027 North-east Monsoon season, focusing on early planning, resource coordination and operational readiness.
In a statement today, Petra said preparations for the Northeast Monsoon, which began on October 27 and is expected to last until March 2027, are being coordinated through the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) to ensure effective and comprehensive flood risk management.
The ministry said the DID National Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre (PRABN) issued 103 bulletins, comprising 64 early flood forecast bulletins and 39 flood warning bulletins, during the 2025/2026 North-east Monsoon season from November 13, 2025, to March 31, 2026.
“Some 14.8 million short message service (SMS) alerts were sent to residents in high-risk areas, according to records from the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC),” the statement said.
“A total of 799 flood incidents were recorded nationwide, comprising 480 monsoon floods, 274 flash floods, 25 cases of stagnant flooding and 20 coastal floods,” it said.
Petra said the flooding was attributed to several factors, including river overflows, internal drainage problems and high tides, as well as localised issues such as blocked drains, uncontrolled development, land clearing and improper waste disposal.
In preparation for the 2026/2027 North-east Monsoon, the DID was carrying out round-the-clock monitoring throughout the year using flood forecasting models covering 36 river basins, supported by 2,237 telemetry-based hydrological stations that record rainfall and river water levels, the ministry said.
The ministry said 614 flood warning sirens and 197 surveillance cameras were also in place at strategic locations nationwide to support flood monitoring and early warning efforts.
Petra said 3,045 locations nationwide had been identified as flood hotspots, having experienced flooding at least three times in the past three years, with Kelantan recording the highest number at 609, followed by Pahang (572) and Terengganu (460).
In terms of operational readiness, the ministry said 1,079 water control gates and 285 pump houses nationwide are in good condition and ready to support flood control operations.
Petra said 580 portable emergency pumps of various capacities were also ready for deployment to critical areas to mitigate flood risks.
Meanwhile, the ministry said 16 DID control dams and 781 flood retention ponds were being monitored, while maintenance work continued in high-risk river basins.
“Cooperation with MCMC and telecommunications companies is ongoing to facilitate the dissemination of flood warnings via SMS to residents in high-risk areas,” it said.
Petra said it was also working with state authorities to establish standard operating procedures (SOPs) for dam water releases to enhance floodwater retention capacity during the Northeast Monsoon season.
To mitigate flood risks, the ministry said 1,638 minor projects were implemented in 2026 at a cost of RM652 million, while 342 development projects under the First Rolling Plan of the 13th Malaysia Plan were approved for implementation this year, with an allocation of RM3.2 billion.
Petra also advised the public to stay informed of official flood forecasts and warnings issued by the DID through the Public InfoBanjir website and MyPublicInfoBanjir mobile application, which is available for download from the Google Play Store and Apple App Store. — Bernama
